diseases.definition: This syndrome is an isolated upper limb mesomelic dysplasia. It has been described in four patients from two unrelated families (a man and his daughter, and a Lebanese man and his son). Patients present with ulnar hypoplasia with severe radial bowing, but normal stature. The mode of transmission is likely to be autosomal dominant with variable expressivity.

diseases.name: Upper limb defect-eye and ear abnormalities syndrome
diseases.definition: Upper limb defect - eye and ear abnormalities syndrome associates upper limb defects (hypoplastic thumb with hypoplasia of the metacarpal bone and phalanges and delayed bone maturation), developmental delay, central hearing loss, unilateral poorly developed antihelix, bilateral choroid coloboma and growth retardation.

diseases.name: Upper gum cancer
synonyms: malignant neoplasm of gingiva of upper jaw
malignant gingiva of upper jaw neoplasm
cancer of gingiva of upper jaw
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|digestive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A cancer involving a gingiva of upper jaw.

diseases.name: Upper clivus meningioma
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A meningioma that affects the upper clivus.

diseases.name: Upper aerodigestive tract neoplasm
diseases.definition: Soft tissue tumors or cancer arising from the mucosal surfaces of the lip; oral cavity; pharynx; larynx; and cervical esophagus. Other sites included are the nose and paranasal sinuses; salivary glands; thyroid gland and parathyroid glands; and melanoma and non-melanoma skin cancers of the head and neck. (from Holland et al., Cancer Medicine, 4th ed, p1651)

diseases.name: Unspecified juvenile idiopathic arthritis
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: Unspecified juvenile idiopathic arthritis is a rare, pediatric, rheumatologic disease, a subtype of juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) characterized by arthritis of an unknown cause that persists for at least 6 weeks, and does not fulfill the criteria for any of the other JIA subtypes, or fulfills criteria for more than one of the other subtypes.

diseases.name: Univentricular heart with single atrio-ventricular valve
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Univentricular heart
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Univentricular heart (UVH) is a severe congenital cardiac malformation characterized by both atria related entirely or almost entirely to one functionally single ventricular chamber. The clinical manifestations include congestive heart failure, failure to thrive, cyanosis, hypoxemia and neurodevelopmental disabilities.

diseases.name: Unilateral retinoblastoma
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A retinoblastoma that only involves a single eye.

diseases.name: Unilateral polymicrogyria
diseases.definition: Unilateral polymicrogyria is a cerebral cortical malformation characterized by unilateral excessive cortical folding and abnormal cortical layering. It comprises two sub-types depending on the areas affected: unilateral hemispheric and focal polymicrogyria.

diseases.name: Unilateral multicystic dysplastic kidney
diseases.group: urinary system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Unilateral multicystic dysplastic kidney is the form of multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK), a congenital anomaly of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT), in which one kidney is large, distended by multiple cysts, and non-functional.

diseases.name: Unilateral focal polymicrogyria
diseases.definition: Unilateral focal polymicrogyria (BFPP) is the mildest sub-type of polymicrogyria (PMG), a cerebral cortical malformation characterized by excessive cortical folding and abnormal cortical layering, that affects only one small region of the brain and that may show no neurologic involvement.

diseases.name: unifocal langerhans cell histiocytosis
diseases.group: immune system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Undifferentiated round cell sarcoma
diseases.definition: An undifferentiated soft tissue sarcoma characterized by the presence of uniform round or ovoid malignant cells with a high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, inflammatory variant
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma characterized by the presence of numerous inflammatory cells.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma
synonyms: malignant fibrous histiocytoma of the soft tissue and bone
malignant fibrous histiocytoma of soft tissue and bone
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An undifferentiated soft tissue sarcoma characterized by the presence of a pleomorphic malignant cellular infiltrate. It is also known as malignant fibrous histiocytoma.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated pancreatic carcinoma with osteoclast-like giant cells
synonyms: undifferentiated pancreatic carcinoma with osteoclast-like giant cells
undifferentiated carcinoma of pancreas with osteoclast-like giant cells
pancreatic undifferentiated carcinoma with osteoclast-like giant cells
osteoclastic giant cell tumour of pancreas
osteoclastic giant cell tumor of pancreas
osteoclast-like giant cell neoplasm of the pancreas
osteoclast-like giant cell neoplasm of pancreas
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare variant of undifferentiated pancreatic carcinoma characterized by the presence of non-neoplastic osteoclast-like giant cells.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated ovarian carcinoma
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An aggressive carcinoma arising from the ovary. Most patients present with advanced disease. Microscopically, it is characterized by significant cytologic atypia, increased mitotic activity, and necrosis. The prognosis is usually poor.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated high grade pleomorphic sarcoma of bone
synonyms: undifferentiated high grade pleomorphic sarcoma of bone
malignant fibrous histiocytoma of the bone
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare, high-grade pleomorphic malignant neoplasm arising from the bone. It usually presents with pain which may or may not be associated with swelling in the affected area. It is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped cells, polygonal or epithelioid cells, multinucleated giant cells, and inflammatory cells. The neoplastic cells exhibit nuclear pleomorphism and high mitotic activity. I...

diseases.name: Undifferentiated gallbladder carcinoma
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A carcinoma without evidence of differentiation arising from the gallbladder. The most common variant is the spindle and giant cell type which resembles a sarcoma.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Embryonal sarcoma of the liver is a rare primary malignant hepatic neoplasm of childhood of mesenchymal origin. It can rarely occur in adults. It is characterized by abdominal mass, right upper quadrant or epigastric pain, nausea, anorexia, intermittent fever or headache.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated connective tissue syndrome
diseases.definition: An autoimmune disorder which does not meet classification criteria used to establish the presence of other well-defined connective tissue diseases.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated carcinoma of the corpus uteri
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Undifferentiated carcinoma of the corpus uteri is a rare cancer of corpus uteri presenting as a large, polypoid, intraluminal mass with necrosis, composed of small to intermediate-size, relatively uniform, dyshesive cells displaying no differentiation. It usually presents with dysfunctional bleeding or vaginal discharge and, less often, abdominal pain. Association with Lynch syndrome was reported.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated carcinoma of stomach
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A carcinoma that arises from the stomach and is characterized by the absence of microscopic features of glandular or squamous differentiation.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated carcinoma of nasopharynx
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|respiratory system disorder|otorhinolaryngologic disease|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A undifferentiated carcinoma that involves the nasopharynx.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated carcinoma of liver and intrahepatic biliary tract
synonyms: undifferentiated carcinoma of liver and IBT
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Undifferentiated carcinoma of liver and intrahepatic biliary tract is an extremely rare epithelial tumor of the liver and biliary tract which presents heterogenous histological findings and not yet fully defined clinicopathological characteristics. Patients usually present with nonspecific signs and symptoms, such as abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, anorexia, weight loss and/or jaundice. Invas...

diseases.name: Undifferentiated carcinoma of esophagus
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|upper digestive tract disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An esophageal carcinoma characterized by the absence of microscopic features of squamous differentiation. However, there is immunohistochemical evidence of squamous differentiation.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated (embryonal) sarcoma
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An aggressive malignant mesenchymal neoplasm that arises from the liver and usually occurs in older children. It is composed of immature spindle, stellate, polymorphous, and giant cells.

diseases.name: Undetermined early-onset epileptic encephalopathy
diseases.definition: A rare infantile epilepsy syndrome characterized by early onset of seizures of variable type and severity, potentially associated with a spectrum of clinical signs and symptoms including delay or lack of psychomotor development, intellectual disability, poor or absent speech development, behavioral abnormalities, hypotonia, movement disorders, spasticity, microcephaly, and dysmorphic facial fea...

diseases.name: Undetermined colitis
diseases.group: hereditary disease|digestive system disorder|immune system disorder
diseases.definition: Underterminate colitis designates a rare inflammatory bowel disease that clinically resembles CrohnBs disease and ulcerative colitis but that cannot be diagnosed as one of them after examination of an intestinal resection specimen.

diseases.name: Uncombable hair syndrome 3
synonyms: uncombable hair syndrome caused by mutation in TCHH
diseases.definition: Any uncombable hair syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TCHH gene.

diseases.name: Uncombable hair syndrome 2
synonyms: uncombable hair syndrome caused by mutation in TGM3
diseases.definition: Any uncombable hair syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TGM3 gene.

diseases.name: Uncombable hair syndrome
diseases.definition: Uncombable hair syndrome (UHS), or pili trianguli et canaliculi, is a rare scalp hair shaft dysplasia.

diseases.name: Unbalanced robertsonian translocation down syndrome
diseases.definition: Robertsonian translocation Down syndrome in which translocation displacement of the end regions of chromosomes occurred with loss of chromosomal material between the two nonhomologous chromosomes.

diseases.name: Umbilical cord ulceration-intestinal atresia syndrome
diseases.definition: Umbilical cord ulceration-intestinal atresia syndrome is characterized by congenital intestinal atresia, umbilical cord ulceration and severe intrauterine hemorrhage.

diseases.name: Ulnar/fibula ray defect-brachydactyly syndrome
diseases.definition: Ulnar/fibula ray defect - brachydactyly syndrome is a very rare malformation syndrome characterized by ulnar hypoplasia associated with hypoplastic to absent fourth and/or fifth digits, fibular hypoplasia, short stature and facial dysmorphism.

diseases.name: Ulnar-mammary syndrome
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Ulnar-mammary syndrome (UMS) is a rare developmental disorder characterized by ulnar defects, mammary and apocrine gland hypoplasia and genital anomalies. Delayed puberty dental anomalies, short stature and obesity have also been described.

diseases.name: Ulnar ray dysgenesis with postaxial polydactyly and renal cystic dysplasia
synonyms: ulnar ray dysgenesis with postaxial polydactyly and renal cystic dysplasia

diseases.name: Ulnar nerve lesion
synonyms: peripheral nerve lesion of ulnar nerve
diseases.definition: A peripheral nerve lesion that involves the ulnar nerve.

diseases.name: Ulnar hypoplasia-split foot syndrome
synonyms: ulnar hypoplasia-lobster-claw deformity of feet syndrome
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Ulnar hypoplasia-split foot syndrome is characterized by the association of severe ulnar hypoplasia, absence of fingers two to five, and split-foot. It has been described in four males belonging to two generations of the same family. X-linked recessive inheritance is suggested, but autosomal dominant transmission cannot be excluded.

diseases.name: Ulnar hemimelia, unilateral
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Ulnar hemimelia, bilateral
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Ulnar hemimelia
synonyms: congenital longitudinal deficiency of the ulna
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Ulnar hemimelia is a congenital ulnar deficiency of the forearm characterized by complete or partial absence of the ulna bone.

diseases.name: Ulna metaphyseal dysplasia syndrome
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Ulna metaphyseal dysplasia syndrome is a rare primary bone dysplasia characterized by dysplasia of the distal ulnar metaphyses, as well as metacarpal/metatarsal dysplasia and metaphyseal changes resembling enchondromata. Patients usually present bony swelling of the wrists with or without pain (knees and ankles may also be affected). Other variably associated features include platyspondyly, ske...

diseases.name: Ulna hypoplasia-intellectual disability syndrome
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Ulna hypoplasia - intellectual deficit is a very rare syndrome characterized by mesomelic shortness of the forearms, bilateral clubfeet, aplasia or hypoplasia of all nails and severe psychomotor retardation.

diseases.name: Ulerythema ophryogenesis
diseases.definition: Ulerythema ophryogenesis is characterized by inflammatory keratotic papules occurring on the face, which may be followed by scars, atrophy and alopecia. Prevalence is unknown but the disease, affecting mainly children and young adults, is rare. Erythema with mild hyperkeratosis of the hair follicles resulting in rough papules is observed on the cheeks and lateral aspects of the eyebrows. The di...

diseases.name: Ulceroglandular tularemia
diseases.definition: A tularemia that results in painful regional lymphadenopathy and an ulcerated skin lesion.

diseases.name: Ulcerative proctosigmoiditis
diseases.group: hereditary disease|digestive system disorder|immune system disorder
diseases.definition: Inflammation of the rectum and the distal portion of the colon.

diseases.name: Ulcerative colitis
diseases.group: hereditary disease|digestive system disorder|immune system disorder|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: An inflammatory bowel disease involving the mucosal surface of the large intestine and rectum. It may present with an acute or slow onset and follows an intermittent or continuous course. Signs and symptoms include abdominal pain, diarrhea, fever, weight loss, and intestinal hemorrhage.

diseases.name: Ulcer of lower limbs
diseases.definition: Ulcer of lower limbs is a chronic ulcer of skin where the ulcer is not a decubitus ulcer.

diseases.name: Tyrosinemia type iii
synonyms: tyrosinemia due to 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvic acid oxidase deficiency
diseases.definition: Tyrosinemia type 3 is an inborn error of tyrosine metabolism characterized by mild hypertyrosinemia and increased urinary excretion of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate, 4-hydroxyphenyllactate and 4-hydroxyphenylacetate.

diseases.name: Tyrosinemia type ii
synonyms: tyrosinemia due to tyrosine aminotransferase deficiency
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|hereditary disease|metabolic disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis|disorder of visual system
diseases.definition: Tyrosinemia type 2 is an inborn error of tyrosine metabolism characterized by hypertyrosinemia with oculocutaneous manifestations and, in some cases, intellectual deficit.

diseases.name: Tyrosinemia type i
diseases.definition: Tyrosinemia type 1 (HTI) is an inborn error of tyrosine catabolism caused by defective activity of fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase (FAH) and is characterized by progressive liver disease, renal tubular dysfunction, porphyria-like crises and a dramatic improvement in prognosis following treatment with nitisinone.

diseases.name: Tyrosinemia
diseases.definition: An autosomal recessive inherited metabolic disorder caused by mutations in the FAH, HPD, and TAT genes. It is characterized by deficiency of one of the enzymes that are involved in the metabolism of tyrosine. It results in elevated blood tyrosine levels and accumulation of tyrosine and its byproducts in the liver, kidney, nervous system and other organs.

diseases.name: Tyrosine hydroxylase deficiency
diseases.definition: Tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by a spectrum of phenotypic features, based on severity and response to levodopa. It can be broadly categorized into TH-deficient dopa-responsive dystonia (mild, with dramatic and sustained response to levodopa), TH-deficiency infantile parkinsonism with motor delay (severe, with incomplete response to levodop...

diseases.name: Typical urticaria pigmentosa
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|immune system disorder|hematologic disorder|inflammatory disease|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Typical nemaline myopathy
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|nervous system disorder
diseases.definition: Typical nemaline myopathy is a moderate neonatal form of nemaline myopathy (NM) characterized by facial and skeletal muscle weakness and mild respiratory involvement.

diseases.name: Typhoidal tularemia
diseases.definition: A tularemia that results in bacteremia and has symptom fever, has symptom chills, has symptom myalgia, has symptom malaise, and has symptom weight loss.

diseases.name: Typhoid fever
diseases.definition: A bacterial infectious disorder contracted by consumption of food or drink contaminated with Salmonella typhi. This disorder is common in developing countries and can be treated with antibiotics.

diseases.name: Type ii mixed cryoglobulinemia
diseases.definition: Type II mixed cryoglobulinemia, a relatively rare clinico-serological subtype of mixed cryoglobulinemia (MC), is an immune complex disorder characterized by purpura, weakness and arthralgia and defined immunochemically by cryoglobulins composed of polyclonal IgGs (autoantigens) and monoclonal IgM (autoantibody).

diseases.name: Type ii hypersensitivity reaction disease
diseases.definition: A disease that has its basis in the disruption of type II hypersensitivity.

diseases.name: Type ii complement component 8 deficiency
synonyms: classic complement early component deficiency caused by mutation in C8B
C8B classic complement early component deficiency
diseases.definition: Any classic complement early component deficiency in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the C8B gene.

diseases.name: Type i complement component 8 deficiency
synonyms: classic complement early component deficiency caused by mutation in C8A
C8A classic complement early component deficiency
diseases.definition: Any classic complement early component deficiency in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the C8A gene.

diseases.name: type 5 diabetes mellitus
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|metabolic disease|endocrine system disorder
diseases.definition: Any diabetes mellitus caused by an inability of the pancreas to produce enough insulin due to underdeveloped pancreatic tissue resulting from prolonged undernutrition.

diseases.name: Type 3 autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare, primary immunodeficiency. It is caused by a currently undetermined defect in the Fas-induced apoptosis pathway. No mutations in Fas, FASLG or CASP10 are detectable. Disruption of Fas-induced apoptosis impairs lymphocyte homeostasis and immune tolerance. Characteristic laboratory findings include an increase in circulating, double-negative (CD4-/CD8-) T cells in the setting of immune-med...

diseases.name: Type 2 papillary adenoma of the kidney
synonyms: type 2 papillary adenoma of the kidney
diseases.group: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|metabolic disease|endocrine system disorder
diseases.definition: A type of diabetes mellitus that is characterized by insulin resistance or desensitization and increased blood glucose levels. This is a chronic disease that can develop gradually over the life of a patient and can be linked to both environmental factors and heredity.

diseases.name: Type 1 papillary adenoma of the kidney
synonyms: type 1 papillary adenoma of the kidney
diseases.group: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|immune system disorder|metabolic disease|endocrine system disorder
diseases.definition: A chronic condition characterized by minimal or absent production of insulin by the pancreas.

diseases.name: Tympanosclerosis
diseases.definition: The formation of dense connective tissue in the tympanic membrane that does not necessarily cause or lead to loss of hearing.

diseases.name: Tympanic paraganglioma
diseases.group: auditory system disorder|hereditary disease|nervous system disorder|endocrine system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis|otorhinolaryngologic disease|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A benign or malignant middle ear paraganglioma arising from paraganglia around the tympanum. Signs and symptoms include a mass behind the tympanum, tinnitus, and conductive hearing loss.

diseases.name: Twin to twin transfusion syndrome
synonyms: foetal blood loss from foetal haemorrhage into co-twin
fetal blood loss from fetal hemorrhage into co-twin
diseases.definition: Twin twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS) is a rare condition seen in twin monochorionic pregnancies, typically developing during the 15-26 week gestation period and usually due to unbalanced intertwin placental anastomoses, where an unequal exchange of blood between twins causes oligohydramnios in one sac and polyhydramnios in the other which can lead to a high perinatal mortality rate and a high ...

diseases.name: Tunnel subaortic stenosis
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Tungiasis
synonyms: Tunga penetrans caused disease or disorder
diseases.definition: An disease or disorder caused by infection with Tunga penetrans.

diseases.name: Tumoral calcinosis, hyperphosphatemic, familial, 3
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|hereditary disease|metabolic disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Tumoral calcinosis, hyperphosphatemic, familial, 2
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|hereditary disease|metabolic disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Tumoral calcinosis, hyperphosphatemic, familial, 1
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|hereditary disease|metabolic disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 11
synonyms: tumour suppressor Gene on chromosome type 11
tumor suppressor Gene on chromosome type 11

diseases.name: Tumor predisposition syndrome 3
synonyms: melanoma, cutaneous malignant, susceptibility to, type 10
malignant glioma caused by mutation in POT1
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Any hereditary cancer predisposition due to variation(s) in the POT1 gene, which confers a predisposition to development of various types of benign and malignant neoplasms.

diseases.name: Tumor predisposition syndrome 2
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An autosomal recessive cancer predisposition syndrome characterized by the onset of various types of tumors or malignancies in young adulthood. The most common clinical manifestations include acute myeloid leukemia (AML), myelodysplastic syndrome, colorectal adenomatous polyposis and carcinoma, and uveal melanoma.

diseases.name: Tumor lysis syndrome
diseases.group: syndromic disease|metabolic disease|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A condition of metabolic abnormalities that result from a spontaneous or therapy-related cytolysis of tumor cells. Tumor lysis syndrome typically occurs in aggressive, rapidly proliferating lymphoproliferative disorders. Burkitt lymphoma and T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia are commonly associated with this syndrome. Metabolic abnormalities include hyperuricemia, lactic acidosis, hyperkalemi...

diseases.name: Tularemia
synonyms: Francisella tularensis caused disease or disorder
diseases.definition: Tularemia is an infection caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis. It is more common in rodents and rabbits but has been found in other animals including domestic cats, sheep, birds, and hamsters. Humans can become infected in several different ways: by handling infected animals, through tick or deer fly bites, by drinking contaminated water, or by inhaling contaminated dust or aerosols....

diseases.name: Tufted angioma
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|cardiovascular disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Tufted angioma is a very rare, benign, cutaneous, slow-growing, vascular tumor mostly developing in infancy or early childhood.

diseases.name: Tubulointerstitial nephritis and uveitis syndrome
synonyms: acute tubulointerstitial nephritis and uveitis syndrome
diseases.definition: An autoimmune disorder comprising tubulointerstitial nephritis and uveitis.

diseases.name: Tubulointerstitial kidney disease, autosomal dominant, 2
synonyms: medullary cystic kidney disease, autosomal dominant
autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease due to mutations in MUC1
autosomal dominant medullary cystic kidney disease without hyperuricemia
MUC1-related autosomal dominant medullary cystic kidney disease
diseases.definition: An inherited disorder that causes a gradual loss of kidney function, caused by a mutation in the MUC1 gene that leads to production of an abnormal mucin 1 protein, which deposits in the kidney and leads to slow loss of kidney function.

diseases.name: Tubulocystic renal cell carcinoma
diseases.group: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Tubulocystic renal cell carcinoma is an extremely rare subtype of renal cell carcinoma most frequently characterized by a small, solitary, well-circumscribed, unencapsulated renal tumor composed of multiple small to medium-sized cysts with a white or gray, spongy ("bubble wrap-like") cut surface. Patients are usually asymptomatic or could manifest with abdominal pain, abdominal distension and/o...

diseases.name: Tubulinopathy-associated dysgyria
synonyms: brain stem asymmetry-superior cerebellar and basal ganglia dysplasia syndrome
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Tubulinopathy
diseases.definition: A nervous system disorder characterized by complex cortical malformations including in most cases dysmorphic basal ganglia and/or corpus callosum in which the cause of the disease is a variation in a tubulin gene.

diseases.name: Tubular variant testicular seminoma
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A morphologic variant of testicular seminoma characterized by the presence of seminoma cells arranged in tubular patterns and few lymphocytes.

diseases.name: Tubular renal disease-cardiomyopathy syndrome
diseases.definition: A syndrome characterized by hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis secondary to a tubulopathy, hypomagnesaemia with hypermagnesuria, severe hypercalciuria and dilated cardiomyopathy.

diseases.name: Tubular duplication of the esophagus
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|upper digestive tract disorder
diseases.definition: Tubular duplication of the esophagous is a rare congenital malformation where a second structure with individual lumen and stratified squamous mucosa and muscularis mucosa lies within or adjacent to the true esophagus causing dysphagia, nausea, vomiting, retrosternal pain and respiratory problems (stridor and recurrent pneumonia) and usually presenting in children.

diseases.name: Tubular aggregate myopathy
diseases.definition: Tubular aggregate myopathy is a disorder that affects the skeletal muscles. Signs and symptoms typically begin in childhood and worsen over time. The leg muscles are most often affected, but the arm muscles may also be involved. Symptoms include muscle pain, cramping, weakness or stiffness; and exercise-induced muscle fatigue. Affected individuals may have an unusual walking style (gait) or dif...

diseases.name: Tuberous sclerosis 2
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An autosomal dominant syndrome caused by pathogenic variants in the TSC2 gene, characterized by the growth of hamartomas in multiple organs, including the brain, skin, kidneys, heart, and lungs. Other clinical features include seizures, intellectual disability, and skin lesions.

diseases.name: Tuberous sclerosis 1
synonyms: tuberous sclerosis caused by mutation in TSC1
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An autosomal dominant syndrome caused by pathogenic variants in the TSC1 gene, characterized by the growth of hamartomas in multiple organs, including the brain, skin, kidneys, heart, and lungs. Other clinical features include seizures, intellectual disability, and skin lesions.

diseases.name: Tuberous sclerosis
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Hereditary disease characterized by seizures, intellectual disability, developmental delay, and skin and ocular lesions. First signs usually occur during infancy or childhood but in rare cases may not occur until 2nd or 3rd decade.

diseases.name: Tuberculum sellae meningioma
synonyms: sella turcica neoplasm of tuberculum sellae
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A meningioma that affects the tuberculum sellae.

diseases.name: Tuberculous pneumothorax
diseases.definition: A pneumothorax caused by tuberculosis infection, typically resulting from rupture of a cavitary tuberculous lesion into the pleural space.

diseases.name: Tuberculous peritonitis
diseases.definition: A form of peritonitis seen in patients with tuberculosis, characterized by lesion either as a miliary form or as a pelvic mass on the peritoneal surfaces. Most patients have ascites, abdominal swelling, abdominal pain, and other systemic symptoms such as fever; weight loss; and anemia.

diseases.name: Tuberculous oophoritis
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|infectious disease|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: An urogenital tuberculosis involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the ovary.

diseases.name: Tuberculous fibrosis of lung
diseases.definition: Scarring of the lung parenchyma caused by pulmonary tuberculosis.

diseases.name: Tuberculous epididymitis
diseases.definition: An urogenital tuberculosis involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the epididymis.

diseases.name: Tuberculous encephalopathy
diseases.definition: A tuberculosis that is characterized by cerebral edema sometimes with features similar to acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) and may manifest with a variety of symptoms ranging from focal neurological deficits to convulsions and decreased conscious state.

diseases.name: Tuberculous empyema
diseases.definition: An empyema resulting from infection by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

diseases.name: Tuberculous ascites
diseases.definition: A type of abdominal tuberculosis that is characterized by accumulation of fluid in the abdomen, a swollen abdomen, and slightly raised tubercles of 1–2 mm all over the peritoneum.

diseases.name: Tuberculosis, spinal
diseases.definition: Tuberculosis of the vertebrae.

diseases.name: Tuberculoma
diseases.definition: A tumor-like mass resulting from the enlargement of a tuberculous lesion.

diseases.name: Tuberculoid leprosy
diseases.definition: A principal or polar form of leprosy in which the skin lesions are few and are sharply demarcated. Peripheral nerve involvement is pronounced and may be severe. Unlike lepromatous leprosy (leprosy, lepromatous), the lepromin test is positive. Tuberculoid leprosy is rarely a source of infection to others.

diseases.name: Tuberculin skin test reactivity, absence of
synonyms: tuberculin skin test reactivity, absence of

diseases.name: Tubal pregnancy
diseases.definition: An abnormal pregnancy in which the conception is implanted in the fallopian tube.

diseases.name: True unicornuate uterus
synonyms: complete unilateral aplasia of the Müllerian ducts
complete unilateral aplasia of the Mullerian ducts
diseases.definition: True unicornuate uterus is a rare, non-syndromic uterovaginal malformation characterized by a crescent-shaped, small-sized uterus containing a single horn and fallopian tube with no rudimentary horn. Urinary tract anomalies are frequently associated.

diseases.name: True myeloschisis
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: A rare open neural tube defect characterized by no other malformation than myeloschisis (spina bifida with a neural placode exposed at or below the skin plane and Chiari II malformation).

diseases.name: True myelomeningocele
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: A rare open neural tube defect characterized by no other malformation than myelomeningocele (spina bifida with a neural placode exposed at the top of a non-epidermised dysplasic meninges sac and Chiari II malformation).

diseases.name: True hermaphroditism
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: A rare condition characterized by the unequivocal presence of both testicular and ovarian tissues in an individual. It is usually manifested with ambiguous external genitalia.

diseases.name: Tropical sprue
diseases.definition: A rare disorder of the digestive tract characterized by malabsorption and anemia. It is likely caused by infection leading to small intestinal mucosal injury, bacterial overgrowth and inflammatory changes. It is most prevalent in residents and visitors to tropical and subtropical climates. Clinical signs include anorexia, abdominal bloating, diarrhea and weight loss. Clinical course may progres...

diseases.name: Tropical spastic paraparesis
synonyms: Human T-lymphotropic virus type-1-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis
Human T-lymphotropic virus type I-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis
diseases.definition: Tropical spastic paraparesis is a chronic systemic immune-mediated inflammatory myeloneuropathy, more frequently reported in women than in men, that usually presents in adulthood with slowly progressive spastic paraparesis of the lower limbs, bladder and bowel dysfunction, and sensory disturbances in the lower extremities (e.g. paresthesia and dysesthesia) and that is associated with a human T-...

diseases.name: Tropical pancreatitis
diseases.group: hereditary disease|digestive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: Tropical pancreatitis is a rare pancreatic disease of juvenile onset occurring mainly in tropical developing countries and characterized by chronic non-alcoholic pancreatitis manifesting with abdominal pain, steatorrhea and fibrocalculous pancreatopathy. It is also commonly associated with the development of pancreatic calculi and pancreatic cancer at a much higher frequency than seen in ordina...

diseases.name: Tropical endomyocardial fibrosis
diseases.definition: Tropical endomyocardial fibrosis is a restrictive cardiopathy, occurring almost exclusively in children and young adults in tropical and subtropical regions, characterized by endocardial fibrosis, affecting the apices and the inflow tract of the right or left ventricle (or both) and manifesting with a restrictive cardimyopathy and atrioventricular regurgitation leading to severe pulmonary hyper...

diseases.name: Trombiculiasis
diseases.definition: Infestation with mites of the genus Trombiculidae, whose larvae carry the rickettsial agent of scrub typhus.

diseases.name: Trochlear nerve neoplasm
synonyms: tumour of the fourth cranial nerve
tumor of the fourth cranial nerve
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A neoplasm involving a trochlear nerve.

diseases.name: Trisomy x
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|chromosomal disorder
diseases.definition: Trisomy X is a sex chromosome anomaly with a variable phenotype caused by the presence of an extra X chromosome in females (47,XXX instead of 46,XX).

diseases.name: Trisomy 9p
synonyms: trisomy of the short arm of chromosome 9
partial trisomy of the short arm of chromosome type 9
partial trisomy of the short arm of chromosome 9
partial duplication of the short arm of chromosome 9
Duplication of the short arm of chromosome 9
diseases.definition: Trisomy 9p is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome, resulting from a partial or complete trisomy of the short arm of chromosome 9, with a wide phenotypic variablility, typically characterized by intellectual disability, craniofacial dysmorphism (e.g. microcephaly, large anterior fontanel, hypertelorism, strabismus, downslanting palpebral fissures, malformed, low-set, protruding ears, bulbous nos...

diseases.name: Trisomy 8q
diseases.definition: Trisomy 8q is a very rare disorder characterized by duplication of the long arm of chromosome 8. The most commonly associated abnormalities include low birth weight, craniofacial abnormalities (prominent forehead, flat occiput, hypertelorism, upslanting palpebral fissures, ear and nose deformities, thin upper lips), congenital heart defects, skeletal defects, psychomotor retardation. Phenotypic...

diseases.name: Trisomy 8p
diseases.definition: Trisomy 8p is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome, resulting from the partial duplication of the short arm of chromosome 8, with highly variable phenotype ranging from no dysmorphic features and only mild intellectual disability to patients with severe developmental delay, neonatal hypotonia, short stature, profound intellectual disability, mild dysmorphic features (e.g. mild ptosis, hypertelor...

diseases.name: Trisomy 5p
synonyms: trisomy of the short arm of chromosome 5
Duplication of the short arm of chromosome 5
diseases.group: chromosomal disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Trisomy 5p is a chromosomal abnormality resulting from the duplication of a segment of variable size of the short arm of chromosome 5, which usually involves the distal band 5p15. The clinical presentation is variable but is always associated with severe intellectual deficit.

diseases.name: Trisomy 4p
synonyms: trisomy of the short arm of chromosome 4
Duplication of the short arm of chromosome 4
diseases.definition: Trisomy 4p is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome, resulting from the partial duplication of the short arm of chromosome 4, with a highly variable phenotype, typically characterized by pre- and postnatal growth delay, psychomotor developmental delay and craniofacial dysmorphism (microcephaly, prominent glabelle, hypertelorism, enlarged ears with abnormal helix and antihelix, bulbous nose with f...

diseases.name: Trisomy 20p
synonyms: partial trisomy of the short arm of chromosome 20
partial duplication of the short arm of chromosome 20
diseases.definition: Trisomy 20p is a chromosomal disorder resulting from duplication of all or part of the short arm of chromosome 20. It is mostly characterized by normal growth, mild to moderate intellectual disability, speech delay, poor coordination and evocative facial features.

diseases.name: Trisomy 1q
diseases.definition: Trisomy 1q is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome, resulting from the partial duplication of the long arm of chromosome 1, with a highly variable phenotype principally characterized by intellectual disability, short stature, craniofacial dysmorphism (incl. macro/microcephaly, prominent forehead, posteriorly rotated, low-set ears, abnormal palpebral fissures, microphthalmia, broad, flat nasal br...

diseases.name: Trisomy 18p
synonyms: trisomy of the short arm of chromosome 18
Duplication of the short arm of chromosome 18
diseases.definition: Trisomy 18p is an extremely rare chromosomal anomaly with a poorly defined clinical phenotype. Reported manifestations include short stature, mild, moderate or severe developmental delay and intellectual disability, variable but mild facial dysmorphism, and epilepsy.

diseases.name: Trisomy 18
diseases.definition: Trisomy 18 is a chromosomal abnormality associated with the presence of an extra chromosome 18 and characterized by growth delay, dolichocephaly, a characteristic facies, limb anomalies and visceral malformations.

diseases.name: Trisomy 17p
diseases.definition: Trisomy 17p is a rare chromosomal abnormality resulting from the duplication of the short arm of chromosome 17 and characterized by pre- and post-natal growth retardation, developmental delay, hypotonia, digital abnormalities, congenital heart defects, and distinctive facial features.

diseases.name: Trisomy 13
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|nervous system disorder|chromosomal disorder|disorder of visual system
diseases.definition: Trisomy 13 is a chromosomal anomaly caused by the presence of an extra chromosome 13 and is characterized by brain malformations (holoprosencephaly), facial dysmorphism, ocular anomalies, postaxial polydactyly, visceral malformations (cardiopathy) and severe psychomotor retardation.

diseases.name: Trisomy 12p
diseases.definition: Trisomy 12p is an extremely rare chromosomal disorder (over 30 cases reported worldwide) characterized by craniofacial malformations (round face, prominent cheeks, high bulging forehead, broad and flat nasal bridge, short nose with anteverted nostrils, long philtrum, prominent and everted lower lip, low-set ears, abnormally folded helix, protuberant antihelix), postnatal growth retardation, men...

diseases.name: Trisomy 10p
diseases.definition: Trisomy 10p is a syndrome of mental retardation/multiple congenital malformations (MR-MCA) that is caused by the total or partial duplication of the short arm of chromosome 10.

diseases.name: Trismus-pseudocamptodactyly syndrome
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Triploidy
diseases.definition: Triploidy is a chromosome abnormality that occurs when there is an extra set of chromosomes present in each cell. Most pregnancies affected by triploidy are lost through early miscarriage. However, reports exist of some affected babies living up to five months. Those that survive are often mosaic. The signs and symptoms associated with triploidy vary but may include a variety of birth defects a...

diseases.name: Triple-positive breast carcinoma
synonyms: hormone receptor positive her2 positive breast cancer
diseases.definition: A breast carcinoma which is positive for expression of estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2).

diseases.name: Triple-a syndrome
diseases.definition: Triple A syndrome is a very rare multisystem disease characterized by adrenal insufficiency with isolated glucocorticoid deficiency, achalasia, alacrima, autonomic dysfunction and neurodegeneration.

diseases.name: Triphalangeal thumbs-brachyectrodactyly syndrome
diseases.definition: Triphalangeal thumbs-brachyectrodactyly syndrome is characterized by triphalangeal thumbs and brachydactyly of the hands. It has been described in four families and in one isolated case. Ectrodactyly of the feet and, more rarely, ectrodactyly of the hands were also reported in some family members. Transmission is autosomal dominant.

diseases.name: Triphalangeal thumb-polysyndactyly syndrome
diseases.group: hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Triphalangeal thumb-polysyndactyly syndrome (TPT-PS) is a hand-foot malformation characterized by triphalangeal thumbs and pre- and postaxial polydactyly, isolated syndactyly or complex polysyndactyly.

diseases.name: Triosephosphate isomerase deficiency
synonyms: hemolytic anemia due to triosephosphate isomerase deficiency
hemolytic anaemia due to triosephosphate isomerase deficiency
diseases.definition: Triosephosphate isomerase (TPI) deficiency is a severe autosomal recessive inherited multisystem disorder of glycolytic metabolism characterized by hemolytic anemia and neurodegeneration.

diseases.name: Triopia
diseases.definition: A craniofacial malformation with prosencephalic duplication; the presence of three eyes.

diseases.name: Triokinase and fmn cyclase deficiency syndrome
Trimethylaminuria
diseases.definition: A rare inborn error of metabolism characterized by the presence of large amounts of trimethylamine in urine, sweat, and breath, resulting in a fishy body odor in affected individuals.

diseases.name: Trilateral retinoblastoma
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Trilateral retinoblastoma refers to bilateral (or less often unilateral) retinoblastoma associated with an intracranial primitive neuroectodermal tumor in the pineal or suprasellar region. This syndrome is often associated with a increased familial incidence of retinoblastoma. (From Cancer 86(1): 135-141, 1999).

diseases.name: Trigonocephaly-short stature-developmental delay syndrome
diseases.definition: A syndrome characterized by short stature, trigonocephaly and developmental delay. It has been described in three males. Moderate intellectual deficit was reported in one of the males and the other two patients displayed psychomotor retardation. X-linked transmission has been suggested but autosomal recessive inheritance can not be ruled out.

diseases.name: Trigonocephaly-broad thumbs syndrome
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Trigonocephaly-broad thumbs syndrome is characterized by neonatal trigonocephaly and multiple anomalies including craniosynostosis, shallow orbits, unusual nose, deviation of the terminal phalanges of fingers 1, 2, and 5, and broad toes with duplication of the terminal phalanx. It has been described in a mother and her son. It is transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait.

diseases.name: Trigonocephaly-bifid nose-acral anomalies syndrome
diseases.definition: Trigonocephaly-bifid nose-acral anomalies syndrome is characterized by trigonocephaly, brachycephaly, bulbous nose (bifid at the tip), micrognathia, macrostomia, hypotonia and relatively broad metatarsals and phalanges.

diseases.name: Trigonocephaly 2
synonyms: isolated trigonocephaly caused by mutation in FREM1
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Any isolated trigonocephaly in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FREM1 gene.

diseases.name: Trigonocephaly 1
synonyms: isolated trigonocephaly caused by mutation in FGFR1
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Any isolated trigonocephaly in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FGFR1 gene.

diseases.name: Trigonitis
synonyms: inflammation of trigone of urinary bladder
diseases.definition: Inflammation of the trigone of the urinary bladder.

diseases.name: triglyceride deposit cardiomyovasculopathy
diseases.definition: A rare cardiovascular disorder characterized by defective intracellular lipolysis of long-chain triglycerides (LCTG), resulting in heart failure and diffuse atherosclerosis.

diseases.name: Trigger thumb
diseases.definition: A painful disability in the hand affecting the finger or thumb. It is caused by mechanical impingement of the digital flexor tendons as they pass through a narrowed retinacular pulley at the level of the metacarpal head. Thickening of the sheath and fibrocartilaginous metaplasia can occur, and nodules can form. (From Green's Operative Hand Surgery, 5th ed, p2137-58).

diseases.name: Trigeminal trophic syndrome
diseases.definition: A syndrome characterized by an uncommon and relatively unknown cause of facial ulceration that occurs after damage to the trigeminal nerve. It characteristically involves non-healing facial ulceration(s) with accompanying anesthesia, paresthesia, and dysesthesia along the distribution of a trigeminal dermatome.

diseases.name: Trigeminal schwannoma
synonyms: schwannoma of the fifth cranial nerve
neurilemmoma of the fifth cranial nerve
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A schwannoma that involves the trigeminal nerve.

diseases.name: Trigeminal neuralgia
diseases.definition: Trigeminal neuralgia is a nerve disorder that causes a stabbing or electric-shock-like pain in parts of the face. The pain lasts a few seconds to a few minutes, and usually on only one side of the face. It can also cause muscle spasms in the face the same time as the pain. The pain may result from a blood vessel pressing against the trigeminal nerve (the nerve that carries pain, feeling, and ot...

diseases.name: Tricuspid valve stenosis
diseases.definition: Narrowing or stricture of the tricuspid orifice of the heart.

diseases.name: Tricuspid valve prolapse
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Abnormal protrusion of one or more of the leaflets of tricuspid valve into the right atrium during systole. This allows the backflow of blood into right atrium leading to tricuspid valve insufficiency; systolic murmurs. Its most common cause is not primary valve abnormality but rather the dilation of the right ventricle and the tricuspid annulus.

diseases.name: Tricuspid valve insufficiency
diseases.definition: The backflow of blood from the right ventricle into the right atrium, owning to imperfect functioning/insufficiency of the tricuspid valve.

diseases.name: Tricuspid valve agenesis
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Tricuspid atresia
diseases.group: hereditary disease|cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Tricuspid atresia is (TA) a rare congenital heart malformation characterized by the congenital agenesis of tricuspid valve leading to severe hypoplasia of right ventricle (functionally univentricular). TA is associated with normally related or transposed great vessels (TGV), an obligatory interatrial connection that is crucial for survival (patent foramen ovale or atrial septal defect, osteum s...

diseases.name: Trichuriasis
synonyms: Trichuris trichiura caused disease or disorder
diseases.definition: An infection that is caused by the nematode Trichuris trichiura, a soil-transmitted helminth, which is transmitted via food and/or water contaminated with the eggs of the worm. Symptoms are usually mild and include abdominal pain, diarrhea, fatigue, and possibly anemia secondary to blood loss in diarrhea.

diseases.name: Trichrome vitiligo
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|immune system disorder|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: Any form of vitiligo characterized by a tan zone of varying width between normal and depigmented skin. This intermediate tan zone has more inflammatory cells, Langerhans cells, and melanophages than vitiliginous or normal skin. The number of melanocytes is greater than in vitiliginous skin but fewer than in normal skin.

diseases.name: Trichotillomania
diseases.definition: A disorder characterized by repetitive pulling out of one's hair resulting in noticeable hair loss; the individual experiences a rising subjective sense of tension before pulling out the hair and a sense of gratification or relief when pulling out the hair.

diseases.name: Trichothiodystrophy 8, nonphotosensitive
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease|nervous system disorder

diseases.name: Trichothiodystrophy 6, nonphotosensitive
synonyms: nonphotosensitive trichothiodystrophy caused by mutation in GTF2E2
diseases.definition: Any nonphotosensitive trichothiodystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the GTF2E2 gene.

diseases.name: Trichothiodystrophy 5, nonphotosensitive
synonyms: nonphotosensitive trichothiodystrophy caused by mutation in RNF113A
diseases.definition: Any nonphotosensitive trichothiodystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the RNF113A gene.

diseases.name: Trichothiodystrophy 4, nonphotosensitive
synonyms: nonphotosensitive trichothiodystrophy caused by mutation in MPLKIP
diseases.definition: A subtype of trichothiodystrophy caused by mutation(s) in the MPLKIP gene, encoding M-phase-specific PLK1-interacting protein.

diseases.name: Trichothiodystrophy 3, photosensitive
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease|metabolic disease

diseases.name: Trichothiodystrophy 2, photosensitive
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease|metabolic disease

diseases.name: Trichothiodystrophy 1, photosensitive
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease|metabolic disease

diseases.name: Trichothiodystrophy
diseases.definition: Trichothiodystrophy or TTD is a heterogeneous group disorders characterized by short, brittle hair with low-sulphur content (due to an abnormal synthesis of the sulfur containing keratins).

diseases.name: Trichostrongylosis
diseases.definition: Infestation with nematode worms of the genus trichostrongylus. Humans become infected by swallowing larvae, usually with contaminated food or drink, although the larvae may penetrate human skin.

diseases.name: Trichostasis spinulosa
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Trichostasis spinulosa (TS) is a condition where instead of one hair protruding from a hair follicle, a bundle or bush of hair come out of a single follicle. This results in elevated, dark spiny papules on the head, face (usually the nose), and trunk. In this condition, there are numerous tiny open pores filled with multiple tiny short hairs, usually only visible with a magnifying glass. TS usu...

diseases.name: Trichorhinophalangeal syndrome type ii
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|musculoskeletal system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease|chromosomal disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Langer-Giedon syndrome, also known as trichorhinophalangeal syndrome type 2, is a very rare, genetic, multiple congenital anomaly disorder characterized by bone abnormalities, distinctive facial features, multiple exostoses, and intellectual disability.

diseases.name: Trichorhinophalangeal syndrome type i
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|musculoskeletal system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease
diseases.definition: An autosomal dominant malformation syndrome caused by mutations in TRPS1 characterized by distinctive craniofacial and skeletal abnormalities. TRPS I patients have sparse scalp hair, bulbous tip of the nose, long flat philtrum, thin upper vermilion border, and protruding ears. Skeletal abnormalities include cone-shaped epiphyses at the phalanges, hip malformations, and short stature.

diseases.name: Trichorhinophalangeal syndrome
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|musculoskeletal system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease

diseases.name: Trichoodontoonychial dysplasia
synonyms: trichoodontoonychial dysplasia with bone deficiency in frontoparietal region
diseases.definition: Trichoodontoonychial dysplasia is a rare ectodermal dysplasia syndrome characterized by severe generalized hypotrichosis, parietal alopecia, secondary anodontia resulting from enamel hypoplasia, onychodystrophy, bone deficiency in the frontoparietal region and skin manifestations (incl. nevus pigmentosus, papules, ephelides, palmoplantar keratosis, supernumerary nipples, abnormal dermatoglyphic...

diseases.name: Trichomonal vulvovaginitis
diseases.group: urinary system disorder|reproductive system disorder|infectious disease|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: An vulvovaginitis caused by infection with Trichomonas vaginalis.

diseases.name: Trichomegaly-retina pigmentary degeneration-dwarfism syndrome
diseases.definition: Trichomegaly-retina pigmentary degeneration-dwarfism syndrome, also known as Oliver-McFarlane syndrome, is an extremely rare genetic disorder characterized by hair abnormalities, severe chorioretinal atrophy, hypopituitarism, short stature, and intellectual disability.

diseases.name: Trichohepatoenteric syndrome 2
synonyms: tricho-hepato-enteric syndrome caused by mutation in SKIV2L
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|connective tissue disorder|digestive system disorder|immune system disorder
diseases.definition: Any tricho-hepato-enteric syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the SKIV2L gene.

diseases.name: Trichohepatoenteric syndrome 1
synonyms: tricho-hepato-enteric syndrome caused by mutation in TTC37
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|connective tissue disorder|digestive system disorder|immune system disorder
diseases.definition: Any tricho-hepato-enteric syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TTC37 gene.

diseases.name: Trichohepatoenteric syndrome
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|connective tissue disorder|digestive system disorder|immune system disorder
diseases.definition: A severe congenital enteropathy manifesting as intractable diarrhea in the first month of life with failure to thrive and associated with facial dysmorphism, hair abnormalities, and, in some cases, immune disorders and intrauterine growth restriction.

diseases.name: Trichofolliculoma
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Trichofolliculoma is a rare benign follicular hamartoma that develops primarily on the face of adults, with a particular predilection for the back of the nose, but also on the neck or scalp. It presents as a solitary hemispheric flesh-colored nodule with a central pore or black dot that may contain a tuft of hair.

diseases.name: Trichoepithelioma, multiple familial, 2
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Trichoepithelioma, multiple familial, 1
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Trichodysplasia-xeroderma syndrome
diseases.definition: Trichodysplasia-xeroderma syndrome is an extremely rare, syndromic hair shaft anomaly characterized by sparse, coarse, brittle, excessively dry and slow-growing scalp hair, sparse axillary and pubic hair, sparse or absent eyelashes and eyebrows and dry skin. Hair shaft analysis shows pili torti, longitudinal splitting, grooves, peeling and scaling. There have been no further descriptions in the...

diseases.name: Trichodysplasia-amelogenesis imperfecta syndrome
diseases.definition: The association of amelogenesis imperfecta and a microscopically typical hair dysplasia has been found in several members of a family in two generations. Transmission is X-linked.

diseases.name: Trichodermodysplasia-dental alterations syndrome
diseases.definition: Trichodermodysplasia-dental alterations syndrome is a rare, genetic ectodermal dysplasia syndrome characterized by sparse, thin, brittle scalp hair, as well as sparse eyebrows, eyelashes, axillary and pubic hair, delayed eruption of deciduous teeth and hypodontia of both dentitions. Mild palmoplantar keratosis, cafC)-au-lait spots on back, mild dystrophy of nails, and tibial deflection of toes ...

diseases.name: Trichodental syndrome
diseases.definition: Trichodental syndrome is characterized by the association of fine, dry and short hair with dental anomalies. It has been described in less than 10 families. The mode of transmission is autosomal dominant.

diseases.name: Tricho-retino-dento-digital syndrome
synonyms: uncombable hair-retinal pigmentary dystrophy-dental anomalies-brachydactyly syndrome
diseases.definition: Tricho-retino-dento-digital syndrome is an autosomal dominant ectodermal dysplasia syndrome, characterized by uncombable hair syndrome, congenital hypotrichosis and dental abnormalities such as oligodontia or hyperdontia, and associated with early-onset cataract, retinal pigmentary dystrophy, and brachydactyly with brachymetacarpia. Furthermore, hyperactivity and a mild intellectual deficit hav...

diseases.name: Tricho-dento-osseous syndrome
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|musculoskeletal system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease
diseases.definition: Tricho-dento-osseous dysplasia (TDO) belongs to the ectodermal dysplasias and is characterized by curly/kinky hair at birth, enamel hypoplasia with discolouration and molar taurodontism, increased overall bone mineral density (BMD) and increased thickness of the cortical bones of the skull.

diseases.name: Trichinellosis
diseases.definition: A zoonotic parasitic disease caused by the consumption of raw or undercooked meat (pork and wild game) infected by nematodes of the genus Trichinella and that is characterized by an enteral (intestinal) phase, that can be asymptomatic or that can manifests with diarrhea, nausea, vomiting and abdominal pain, and a parenteral (muscular) phase, manifesting with fever, periorbital edema, muscle swe...

diseases.name: Triatrial heart
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: A rare congenital abnormality of the heart characterized by the presence of three atria. The right or left atrium is divided into two parts by fibromuscular tissue or a membrane. It may be associated with other heart congenital abnormalities.

diseases.name: Trench fever
synonyms: bartonellosis due to Bartonella quintana infection
Bartonella quintana caused disease or disorder
diseases.definition: An intermittent fever characterized by intervals of chills, fever, and splenomegaly each of which may last as long as 40 hours. It is caused by bartonella quintana and transmitted by the human louse.

diseases.name: Tremor-ataxia-central hypomyelination syndrome
diseases.group: hereditary disease|nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system

diseases.name: Tremor, hereditary essential, and idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus
synonyms: tremor, hereditary essential, and idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus

diseases.name: Tremor, hereditary essential, 5
synonyms: essential tremor caused by mutation in TENM4
diseases.definition: Any essential tremor in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TENM4 gene.

diseases.name: Tremor, hereditary essential, 4
synonyms: essential tremor caused by mutation in FUS
diseases.definition: Any essential tremor in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FUS gene.

diseases.name: Tremor, hereditary essential, 1
synonyms: essential tremor caused by mutation in DRD3
diseases.definition: Any essential tremor in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the DRD3 gene.

diseases.name: Tremor of intention, ataxia, and lipofuscinosis
synonyms: tremor of intention, ataxia, and lipofuscinosis

diseases.name: Treatment-refractory schizophrenia
diseases.definition: Schizophrenia which does not respond to commonly used treatments.

diseases.name: Traumatic myositis ossificans
diseases.definition: Myositis Ossificans resulting from trauma.

diseases.name: Traumatic encephalopathy
diseases.definition: Encephalopathy resulting from trauma.

diseases.name: Traumatic brain injury
diseases.definition: A brain disease that is characterized by brain dysfunction caused by an outside force, usually a violent blow to the head.

diseases.name: Transverse vaginal septum
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: A rare vaginal malformation characterized by the presence of a complete or incomplete transverse septum at any level of the vagina (most frequently the upper or middle third), resulting from incomplete fusion between the Müllerian duct component and the urogenital sinus component of the vagina during embryogenesis. The condition is only rarely diagnosed in neonates or infants, unless it causes ...

diseases.name: Transverse colon cancer
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A malignant neoplasm involving the transverse colon.

diseases.name: Transketolase deficiency
synonyms: short stature-developmental delay-congenital heart defect syndrome
diseases.group: hereditary disease|cardiovascular disorder|metabolic disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Transitional meningioma
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A WHO grade I meningioma characterized by the coexistence of meningothelial cells and fibrous architectural patterns.

diseases.name: Transitional extramedullary conus spinal cord lipoma
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|nervous system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare form of extramedullary conus region spinal cord lipoma characterized by a location at the posterior surface of the conus and its tip. i.e-"transitional" between posterior and terminal conus region spinal cord lipoma.

diseases.name: Transitional cell carcinoma of the corpus uteri
synonyms: body of uterus transitional cell carcinoma
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A transitional cell carcinoma that involves the body of uterus.

diseases.name: Transient tyrosinemia of the newborn
diseases.definition: A benign disorder of tyrosine metabolism detected upon newborn screening and often observed in premature infants. It shows no clinical symptoms. It is characterized by tyrosinemia, moderate hyperphenylalaninemia, and tyrosiluria that usually resolve after 2 months of age.

diseases.name: Transient tic disorder
diseases.definition: A neurological disorder presenting in childhood that is characterized by motor and/or phonic tics that occur daily or nearly daily for one to twelve months and are not attributed to an identifiable cause.

diseases.name: Transient retinal arterial occlusion
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system
diseases.definition: A partial, temporary occlusion of the retinal artery.

diseases.name: Transient pseudohypoaldosteronism
diseases.definition: Transient pseudohypoaldosteronism is a renal tubulopathy characterized by renal tubular resistance to aldosterone, characterized by hyponatremia, metabolic acidosis and hyperkalemia and manifesting as dehydration, secondary to urinary tract malformation and infections in infants.

diseases.name: Transient neonatal myasthenia gravis
diseases.definition: Transient neonatal myasthenia gravis (MG) is a rare form of MG occurring in neonates born to mothers who have the disorder or specific circulating autoantibodies.

diseases.name: Transient neonatal multiple acyl-coa dehydrogenase deficiency
diseases.definition: Transient neonatal multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency describes a very rare condition where a maternal riboflavin deficiency causes an infant to present with manifestations similar to those seen in multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MAD) deficiency such as poor suck, metabolic acidosis and hypoglycemia, but that resolves completely with oral riboflavin. In the one patient described haploi...

diseases.name: Transient myeloproliferative syndrome
synonyms: Transient abnormal myelopoiesis associated with Down syndrome
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|immune system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A myeloid proliferation occurring in newborns with Down syndrome. It is clinically and morphologically indistinguishable from acute myeloid leukemia and is associated with GATA1 mutations. The blasts display morphologic and immunophenotypic features of megakaryocytic lineage. In the majority of patients the myeloid proliferation undergoes spontaneous remission.

diseases.name: Transient infantile hypertriglyceridemia and hepatosteatosis
synonyms: transient infantile hypertriglyceridemia and fatty liver
diseases.group: hereditary disease|digestive system disorder|endocrine system disorder

diseases.name: Transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|immune system disorder|hematologic disorder
diseases.definition: A rare, primary humoral immunodeficiency of childhood characterized by decreasing serum levels of immunoglobulin G (IgG) as maternal antibodies clear the circulation while serum levels of immunoglobulin A and immunoglobulin M remain normal or are slightly decreased. Diagnosis may be suspected after the age of six months when a child's own synthesis of IgG should accelerate but it must be confir...

diseases.name: Transient hypogammaglobulinemia
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|immune system disorder|hematologic disorder
diseases.definition: A broad classification for humoral immunodeficiencies. These disorders may be caused by inadequate activation of progenitor B cells, defective class-switching or the effects of medications. Despite the potential for increased susceptibility to infection, these disorders are self-limited with eventual normalization of serum antibody levels.

diseases.name: Transient global amnesia
diseases.definition: A condition characterized by sudden, temporary, usually short-lived memory loss, not associated with a neurologic disorder. Affected individuals lose memory function for recent events and have a decreased ability to retain new information. It is usually a solitary event.

diseases.name: Transient familial neonatal hyperbilirubinemia
diseases.group: hereditary disease|digestive system disorder|metabolic disease|endocrine system disorder

diseases.name: Transient erythroblastopenia of childhood
synonyms: transient acquired pure red cell aplasia
diseases.definition: An acquired pure red cell aplasia that is self-limited. It is the most common cause of decreased red blood cell production in the pediatric population, and typically presents as a normocytic anemia with reticulocytopenia in an otherwise asymptomatic and normal child with no evidence of other causes for anemia, including blood loss, hemolysis, nutritional deficiency, or malignancy.

diseases.name: Transient congenital hypothyroidism due to neonatal factor
Transient bullous dermolysis of the newborn
synonyms: transient bullous dermolysis of the newborn
DEB, bullous dermolysis of the newborn
diseases.definition: Transient bullous dermolysis of the newborn is a rare subtype of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (DEB) characterized by generalized blistering at birth that usually regresses within the first 6 to 24 months of life.

diseases.name: Transient arthritis
diseases.definition: Arthritis that is not permanent.

diseases.name: Transgrediens et progrediens palmoplantar keratoderma
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Transcobalamin ii deficiency
diseases.group: hereditary disease|immune system disorder|metabolic disease|nutritional disorder|hematologic disorder
diseases.definition: Transcobalamin deficiency (TC) is a disorder of cobalamin transport that usually presents during the first few months of life and is characterized by megaloblastic anemia, failure to thrive, vomiting, weakness and pancytopenia.

diseases.name: Transaldolase deficiency
diseases.definition: Transaldolase deficiency is an inborn error of the pentose phosphate pathway that presents in the neonatal or antenatal period with hydrops fetalis, hepatosplenomegaly, hepatic dysfunction, thrombocytopenia, anemia, and renal and cardiac abnormalities.

diseases.name: Trachoma
diseases.definition: A chronic infection of the conjunctiva and cornea caused by chlamydia trachomatis.

diseases.name: Tracheobronchopathia osteochondroplastica
diseases.definition: Tracheobronchopathia osteochondroplastica (TO) is an idiopathic and benign disease of the large airways characterized by submucosal osteocartilaginous nodules presenting in the trachea with or without the involvement of the major bronchi.

diseases.name: Tracheitis
diseases.definition: A tracheal disease which involves bacterial infection of the trachea often caused by Staphylococcus aureus and streptococci that follows a recent viral upper respiratory infection. The symptoms include barking croup cough, loud squeaking noise while breathing, scratchy feeling in the throat, high fever, and production of large amounts of pus-filled secretions.

diseases.name: Tracheal stenosis
diseases.definition: Narrowing of the lumen of the trachea.

diseases.name: Tracheal lymphoma
diseases.group: respiratory system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare lymphoma that arises from the trachea. Signs and symptoms include dyspnea, cough, wheezing, and stridor.

diseases.name: Tracheal calcification
diseases.definition: Abnormal deposits of calcium in the tracheal tissue.

diseases.name: Tracheal agenesis
diseases.group: respiratory system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis|otorhinolaryngologic disease
diseases.definition: Tracheal agenesis (TA) is a rare congenital malformation in which the trachea may be completely absent (agenesis), or partially in place but underdeveloped (atresia). In both cases, proximal-distal communication between the larynx and the alveoli of the lungs is lacking.

diseases.name: Tracheal adenoid cystic carcinoma
synonyms: adenoid cystic carcinoma of the trachea
diseases.group: respiratory system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An adenoid cystic carcinoma that arises from the trachea. It spreads to the submucosal tracheal tissue and to regional lymph nodes.

diseases.name: Trachea sarcoma
diseases.group: respiratory system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare malignant soft tissue neoplasm that arises from the trachea.

diseases.name: Trachea mucoepidermoid carcinoma
diseases.group: respiratory system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A mucoepidermoid carcinoma that involves the trachea.

diseases.name: Trachea leiomyoma
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|respiratory system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A benign smooth muscle neoplasm arising from the trachea. It is characterized by the presence of spindle cells with cigar-shaped nuclei, interlacing fascicles, and a whorled pattern.

diseases.name: Trachea carcinoma in situ
synonyms: carcinoma in situ of the trachea
diseases.group: respiratory system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A carcinoma that arises from the tracheal mucosa and is confined to the epithelial layer without evidence of further tissue invasion.

diseases.name: Trabecular follicular adenocarcinoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Trabecular adenocarcinoma
diseases.definition: A malignant epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of a trabecular glandular architectural pattern.

diseases.name: Toxocariasis
diseases.definition: A parasitic infection caused by worms found in domestic animals. In humans nematode larvae enter the portal system from the small intestine and disseminate in visceral organs causing inflammatory reactions. Signs and symptoms include eosinophilia, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and lung infections.

diseases.name: Toxin-mediated infectious botulism
diseases.definition: Aform of botulism (see this term), a rare acquired neuromuscular junction disease, characterized by descending flaccid paralysis caused by botulinum neurotoxins (BoNTs), produced in vivo leading to toxin-mediated infection. Infectious botulism includes wound botulism and intestinal toxemia botulism (infant botulism and adult intestinal botulism).

diseases.name: Toxicodendron dermatitis
synonyms: contact dermatitis due to genus Toxicodendron
