diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|immune system disorder|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: An allergic contact dermatitis caused by exposure to plants of the genus Toxicodendron (formerly Rhus). These include poison ivy, poison oak, and poison sumac, all plants that contain the substance urushiol, a potent skin sensitizing agent. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

diseases.name: toxic thyroid adenoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A condition in which a single benign adenoma on the thyroid gland  autonomously secretes excessive thyroid hormone, leading to primary hyperthyroidism.

diseases.name: Toxic shock syndrome
diseases.definition: A rare acute life-threatening systemic bacterial noncontagious illness caused by exotoxins from bacteria of either the Streptococcus pyogenes or Staphylococcus aureus type. It is characterized by high fever, hypotension, rash, multi-organ dysfunction, and cutaneous desquamation during the early convalescent period. The toxins affect the host immune system, causing an exuberant and pathological ...

diseases.name: Toxic pneumonitis
diseases.definition: A pneumonia that is an acute inflammation of the lungs induced by inhalation of metal fumes or toxic gasses and vapors. It is a sentinel health event (occupational) associated with exposure to ammonia (refrigeration, fertilizer, and oil refining industries), chlorine (alkali and bleach industries), nitrogen oxides (silo fillers, arc welders, and nitric acid industry), sulfur dioxide (paper, ref...

diseases.name: Toxic or nutritional optic neuropathy
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|inflammatory disease|disorder of visual system
diseases.definition: A disease with basis in optic nerve damage secondary to a toxic substance and/or nutritional deficiency.

diseases.name: Toxic optic neuropathy
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|inflammatory disease|disorder of visual system

diseases.name: Toxic oil syndrome
diseases.definition: Toxic oil syndrome is a rare intoxication, due to consumption of a rapeseed oil denatured with aniline 2%, characterized by generalized vascular lesions affecting all organs and vessels (including veins and arteries) and presenting with severe incapacitating myalgias, marked peripheral eosinophilia and pulmonary infiltrates.

diseases.name: Toxic multinodular goitre
diseases.definition: Nodular enlargement of the thyroid gland associated with hyperthyroidism.

diseases.name: Toxic megacolon
diseases.definition: An acute form of megacolon, severe pathological dilatation of the colon. It is associated with clinical conditions such as ulcerative colitis; crohn disease; amebic dysentery; or clostridium enterocolitis.

diseases.name: Toxic maculopathy due to antimalarial drugs
diseases.definition: Toxic maculopathy due to antimalarial drugs is a rare, acquired eye disease, due to long-term exposure to chloroquinine (CQ) or hydrochloroquinine (HCQ), characterized by a slowly progressive, usually non-reversible, development of bilateral atrophic bull's-eye maculopathy (progressive loss of central vision acuity, reduced color vision and central scotoma), which in severe cases can spread ove...

diseases.name: Toxic maculopathy
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system

diseases.name: Toxic labyrinthitis
diseases.definition: A labyrinthitis induced by alcohol, drug ingestion, or occasionally, inhaled substances that are toxic to the inner ear. Drugs like aminoglycosides, furosemide, ethacrynic acid, acetylsalicylic acid, amiodarone, quinine, cisplatin, barbiturates, quinine, anti-Alzheimer's medications, anticonvulsants, antidepressants, and anxiolytics can be ototoxic.

diseases.name: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
diseases.definition: Toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) is an acute and severe skin disease with clinical and histological features characterized by the destruction and detachment of the skin epithelium and mucous membranes.

diseases.name: Toxic bronchiolitis obliterans
diseases.definition: Toxic bronchiolitis whereby a biospy has shown an obliteration of broncioles.

diseases.name: Toxic amblyopia
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system
diseases.definition: A condition where a toxic reaction in the optic nerve results in visual loss. Various poisonous substances may cause the condition as well as nutritional factors.

diseases.name: Toxascariasis
diseases.definition: Infections with nematodes of the genus toxascaris.

diseases.name: Totally drug-resistant tuberculosis
diseases.definition: A type of drug-resistant tuberculosis that is resistant to all first- and second-line antitubercular drugs tested (isoniazid, rifampicin, streptomycin, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, ethionamide, para-aminosalicylic acid, cycloserine, ofloxacin, amikacin, ciprofloxacin, capreomycin, kanamycin).

synonyms: third or oculomotor nerve palsy, total
third nerve palsy with pupil involved

diseases.group: syndromic disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Torticollis-keloids-cryptorchidism-renal dysplasia syndrome is an extremely rare developmental defect during embryogenesis malformation syndrome characterized by congenital muscular torticollis associated with skin anomalies (such as multiple keloids, pigmented nevi, epithelioma), urogenital malformations (including cryptorchidism and hypospadias) and renal dysplasia (e.g. chronic pyelonephriti...

diseases.name: Torsion dystonia with onset in infancy
synonyms: torsion dystonia with onset in infancy
diseases.definition: A dystonia characterized by autosomal dominant inheritance of generalized dystonia with severe involvement of the legs, mild involvement of the face and arms, and onset in infancy.

diseases.name: Torsion dystonia 7
diseases.definition: A focal dystonia characterized by predominately cervical dystonia that has material basis in variation in the chromosome region 18p.

diseases.name: Torsion dystonia 6
synonyms: idiopathic torsion dystonia of mixed type
generalized isolated dystonia caused by mutation in THAP1
generalised isolated dystonia caused by mutation in THAP1
diseases.definition: Primary dystonia DYT6 type is characterized by focal, predominantly cranio-cervical dystonia with dysarthria and dysphagia, or limb dystonia in some cases.

diseases.name: Torsion dystonia 4
diseases.definition: DYT4 type primary dystonia is characterized by predominantly laryngeal dystonia (manifesting as whispering dysphonia) and cervical dystonia (manifesting as torticollis).

diseases.name: Torsion dystonia 2
synonyms: dystonic disorder caused by mutation in HPCA
diseases.definition: A dystonia characterized by segmental dystonia that predominantly affects the distal limbs and leads to abnormal posture. This disease has a progressive clinical course and may develop into generalized dystonia but remains mild overall.

diseases.name: Torsion dystonia 17
diseases.definition: A dystonia characterized by autosomal recessive inheritance of progressive dystonia, dysphonia, dysarthria and neck torticollis that has material basis in variation in the chromosome region 20p11.2-q13.12.

diseases.name: Torsion dystonia 13
synonyms: primary torsion dystonia with predominant craniocervical or upper limb onset
diseases.definition: DYT13 type primary dystonia is characterized by focal or segmental dystonia with cranial, cervical, or upper limb involvement.

diseases.name: Torsades de pointes
diseases.definition: A malignant form of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia that is characterized by heart rate between 200 and 250 beats per minute, and qrs complexes with changing amplitude and twisting of the points. The term also describes the syndrome of tachycardia with prolonged ventricular repolarization, long qt intervals exceeding 500 milliseconds or bradycardia. Torsades de pointes may be self-limited o...

diseases.name: Torsade-de-pointes syndrome with short coupling interval
diseases.definition: Torsade-de-pointes (TdP) syndrome with short coupling interval is a very rare variant of Torsade de pointes, a polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, which is characterized by a short coupling interval of the first TdP beat on electrocardiogram in the absence of any structural heart disease. It manifests in early adulthood with syncope, often results in ventricular fibrillation and shows a high r...

diseases.name: Torpedo maculopathy
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system

diseases.name: Torovirus infectious disease
diseases.definition: Infections with viruses of the genus torovirus, family coronaviridae.

diseases.name: Topographical agnosia
diseases.group: psychiatric disorder|nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system
diseases.definition: An agnosia that is a loss of the ability to rely on visual cues to guide them directionally due to the inability to recognize objects.

diseases.name: Tooth ankylosis
diseases.definition: Dental ankylosis is a rare disorder characterized by the fusion of the tooth to the bone, preventing both eruption and orthodontic movement.

diseases.name: Tooth and nail syndrome
diseases.definition: Hypodontia-nail dysplasia syndrome is a form of ectodermal dysplasia.

tooth agenesis caused by mutation in EDA

diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|musculoskeletal system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease

diseases.name: Tooth agenesis, selective, 3
synonyms: tooth agenesis caused by mutation in PAX9
diseases.definition: Any tooth agenesis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the PAX9 gene.

diseases.name: Tooth agenesis, selective, 1
synonyms: tooth agenesis, selective, 1, with or without orofacial cleft
tooth agenesis caused by mutation in MSX1
MSX1-related tooth agenesis with or without orofacial cleft
diseases.definition: Any tooth agenesis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the MSX1 gene characterized by varying severity of tooth agenesis that may be seen in combination with orofacial clefting in some individuals.

diseases.name: Tooth agenesis
diseases.definition: A tooth disease characterized by failure to develop one or more missing teeth.

diseases.name: Tonsillitis
diseases.group: immune system disorder|respiratory system disorder|inflammatory disease|otorhinolaryngologic disease
diseases.definition: Inflammation of the tonsillar tissue.

diseases.name: Tonsillar squamous cell carcinoma
synonyms: squamous cell carcinoma of the tonsil
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|immune system disorder|respiratory system disorder|otorhinolaryngologic disease|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the mucosal lining of the tonsil and tends to metastasize early to the lymph nodes. It predominantly affects middle aged and elderly patients who have a history of alcohol and tobacco use. Patients may present with tonsillar swelling, sore throat, pain radiating to the ipsilateral ear, or a neck mass.

diseases.name: Tonsillar pillar cancer
synonyms: malignant neoplasm of tonsillar pillars, posterior
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|digestive system disorder|immune system disorder|respiratory system disorder|otorhinolaryngologic disease|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A cancer that involves the tonsillar pillar.

diseases.name: Tonsillar lymphoma
diseases.group: hereditary disease|digestive system disorder|immune system disorder|respiratory system disorder|hematologic disorder|otorhinolaryngologic disease|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A primary lymphoma that affects the tonsil and the bulk of the tumor is in this anatomic area. The majority of cases are B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas.

diseases.name: Tonsillar lipoma
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|immune system disorder|respiratory system disorder|otorhinolaryngologic disease|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A benign adipose tissue neoplasm of the tonsils.

diseases.name: Tonsillar fossa cancer
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|immune system disorder|respiratory system disorder|otorhinolaryngologic disease|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A cancer involving a tonsillar fossa.

diseases.name: Tongue carcinoma
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Toluene embryopathy
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Toluene embryopathy is a neurodevelopmental teratologic syndrome due to prenatal exposure to toluene. The disease is characterized by prematurity, low birth weight, dysmorphic features (short palpebral fissures, deep set eyes, low set ears, mid-facial hypoplasia, flat nasal bridge, thin upper lip, micrognathia, spatulate fingertips and small fingernails), central nervous system dysfunctions (in...

diseases.name: Toes, space between first and second
synonyms: toes, space between first and second

diseases.name: Toes, relative length of first and second
synonyms: toes, relative length of first and second

diseases.name: Toe, fifth, number of phalanges 1n
synonyms: toe, fifth, number of phalanges type 1N

diseases.name: Titinopathy with congenital contractures
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|nervous system disorder
diseases.definition: A prenatal/infant-onset muscle disorder characterized by limb contractures, muscle weakness (often with significant axial involvement), long bone fractures, and/or cardiac abnormalities.

diseases.name: Tinea unguium
synonyms: cellulitis and abscess of upper arm and forearm
cellulitis and abscess of gluteal region
cellulitis and abscess of finger and toe
diseases.definition: A fungal infection of the nail, usually caused by dermatophytes; yeasts; or nondermatophyte molds.

diseases.name: Tinea profunda
diseases.definition: A dermatophytosis that involves the deep dermal layers.

diseases.name: Tinea pedis
diseases.definition: Dermatological pruritic lesion in the feet, caused by Trichophyton rubrum, T. mentagrophytes, or Epidermophyton floccosum.

diseases.name: Tinea nigra
diseases.definition: A superficial mycosis that is a superficial fungal infection of the skin characterized by brown to black macules which usually occur on the palmar aspects of hands and occasionally the plantar and other surfaces of the skin, caused by Hortaea werneckii, which is a common saprophytic fungus believed to occur in soil, compost, humus and on wood in humid tropical and sub-tropical regions.

diseases.name: Tinea manuum
diseases.definition: A dermatophytosis that involves the hands.

diseases.name: Tinea imbricata
diseases.definition: A tinea corporis that results in fungal infection located in skin, has material basis in Trichophyton concentricum, which is characterized by ring-like growth in overlapping circles that may have an autosomal dominant genetic predisposition.

diseases.name: Tinea favosa
diseases.definition: A severe, chronic fungal skin infection, usually of the scalp, characterized by the development of thick, yellow cup-shaped crusts and scarring over hair follicles.

diseases.name: Tinea corporis
diseases.definition: A dermatophyte disease of the glabrous skin, excluding the scalp, beard, face, hands, feet, and groin.

diseases.name: Tinea barbae
diseases.definition: A dermatophytosis that involves the beard.

diseases.name: Time agnosia
diseases.definition: An agnosia that is a loss of the ability to comprehend the succession and duration of events.

diseases.name: Tick-borne relapsing fever
diseases.definition: An infection that is caused by certain species of Rickettsia or Borrelia, which are transmitted to humans from infected ticks; it is characterized by sudden fever, chills, headaches, myalgia, arthralgia, nausea, and possibly a rash. Symptoms usually persist for two to nine days, then disappear, with recurrence after several weeks if the patient remains untreated.

diseases.name: Tick-borne encephalitis
diseases.definition: Tick-borne encephalitis is caused by an arbovirus of the Flaviviridae family (tick-borne encephalitis virus, TBEV), transmitted principally by the bite of the Ixodes ricinus tick. The symptomology is biphasic, with the initial phase being associated with a flu-like illness and the second phase (occurring in less than 10% of patients) with symptoms of meningitis or, more rarely, meningoencephali...

diseases.name: Tick paralysis
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|nervous system disorder|infectious disease
diseases.definition: Paralysis caused by a neurotropic toxin secreted by the salivary glands of ticks.

diseases.name: Tibio-fibular synostosis
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Tibio-fibular synostosis is a rare, non-syndromic limb malformation characterized by fusion of the proximal or distal tibial and fibular metaphysis and/or diaphysis, frequently associated with distal positioning of the proximal tibiofibular joint, leg length discrepancy, bowing of the fibula, and valgus deformity of the knee.

diseases.name: Tibialis tendinitis
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: A tendinitis that involves the tibialis.

diseases.name: Tibial muscular dystrophy
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|nervous system disorder
diseases.definition: A distal myopathy characterized by weakness of the muscles of the anterior compartment of lower limbs, appearing in the fourth to seventh decade of life.

diseases.name: Tibial hemimelia, unilateral
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Tibial hemimelia, bilateral
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Tibial hemimelia
synonyms: congenital longitudinal deficiency of the tibia
congenital aplasia and dysplasia of the tibia with intact fibula
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Tibial hemimelia is a rare congenital anomaly characterized by deficiency of the tibia with a relatively intact fibula.

diseases.name: Tibial aplasia-ectrodactyly syndrome
synonyms: tibial hemimelia with split hand/foot malformation
split-hand/foot malformation associated with aplasia of long bones
split hand/foot malformation with long bone deficiency
aplasia of tibia with split-hand/split-foot deformity
SHFM associated with aplasia of long bones
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Tibial aplasia-ectrodactyly syndrome is a rare condition characterized by congenital ectrodactylous limb malformations associated with tibial aplasia or hypoplasia.

diseases.name: Tibial adamantinoma
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An adamantinoma arising from the tibia. The tibia is the site which is more frequently involved by adamantinoma (80-90% of cases).

diseases.name: Tibia, hypoplasia or aplasia of, with polydactyly
synonyms: tibia, hypoplasia or aplasia of, with polydactyly
hypoplastic or aplastic tibia with polydactyly
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Tibial hemimelia-polysyndactyly-triphalangeal thumb syndrome is a rare, genetic dysostosis syndrome, with marked inter- and intra-familial variation, typically characterized by triphalangeal thumbs, hand and/or foot polysyndactyly and/or absent/hypoplastic tibiae (associated with duplication of fibulae in some cases), although isolated triphalangeal thumbs have also been reported. It is often a...

diseases.name: Tibia, absence of, with congenital deafness
synonyms: tibia, absence of, with congenital deafness

diseases.name: Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis
diseases.definition: Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis (TPP) is a rare neurological disease characterized by recurrent episodes of paralysis and hypokalemia during a thyrotoxic state.

diseases.name: Thyroid malformation
diseases.definition: An anatomic abnormality of the thyroid gland.

diseases.name: Thyroid lymphoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A lymphoma primarily involving the thyroid gland.

diseases.name: Thyroid hypoplasia
diseases.definition: Thyroid hypoplasia is a form of thyroid dysgenesis characterized by incomplete development of the thyroid gland that results in primary congenital hypothyroidism, a permanent thyroid deficiency that is present from birth.

diseases.name: Thyroid hyalinizing trabecular adenoma
synonyms: hyalinizing trabecular adenoma of the thyroid
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare, circumscribed or encapsulated tumor arising from the follicular cells of the thyroid gland. It is characterized by a trabecular growth pattern and hyalinized stroma formation. The vast majority of cases have a benign clinical course.

diseases.name: Thyroid hormone resistance, generalized, autosomal recessive
synonyms: thyroid hormone resistance, generalized, autosomal recessive
diseases.definition: A rare, autosomal recessive inherited disorder usually caused by mutations in the THRB gene. It is characterized by a defective physiological resistance to thyroid hormones, resulting in the elevation of thyroxin and triiodothyronine in the serum.

diseases.name: Thyroid hormone resistance, generalized, autosomal dominant
synonyms: thyroid hormone resistance, generalized, autosomal dominant

diseases.name: Thyroid hormone plasma membrane transport defect
synonyms: thyroid hormone resistance due to T4 plasma Membrane transport defect
thyroid hormone plasma membrane transport defect
hyperthyroxinemia, Eumetabolic, due to T4 plasma Membrane Transport defect

diseases.name: Thyroid hormone metabolism, abnormal 1
synonyms: short stature-delayed bone age due to thyroid hormone metabolism deficiency
diseases.definition: A rare, genetic congenital hypothyroidism disorder characterized by mild global developmental delay in childhood, short stature, delayed bone age, and abnormal thyroid and selenium levels in serum (high total and free T4 concentrations, low T3, high reverse T3, normal to high TSH, decreased selenium). Intellectual disability, primary infertility, hypotonia, muscle weakness, and impaired hearing...

diseases.name: Thyroid hemiagenesis
diseases.definition: Thyroid hemiagenesis is a form of thyroid dysgenesis characterized by an absence of half of the thyroid gland that is usually asymptomatic but may result in primary congenital hypothyroidism, a permanent thyroid deficiency that is present from birth.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland undifferentiated (anaplastic) carcinoma
synonyms: undifferentiated carcinoma of the thyroid gland
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A primary carcinoma of the thyroid gland composed of undifferentiated cells. The malignant cells demonstrate evidence of epithelial differentiation, either by immunohistochemistry or electron microscopic studies. Microscopically, in the majority of cases there is a mixture of spindle, epithelioid, and giant cells. The vast majority of the patients present with a rapidly enlarging neck mass. The...

diseases.name: Thyroid gland squamous cell carcinoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rapidly growing primary carcinoma of the thyroid gland composed of malignant squamous cells. The clinical course is usually aggressive.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland spindle cell tumor with thymus-like differentiation
synonyms: spindle epithelial tumour with thymus-like differentiation tumour
spindle epithelial tumor with thymus-like differentiation tumor
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare, slow growing, primary carcinoma of the thyroid gland characterized by a lobulated architectural pattern and the presence of a biphasic cellular population composed of spindle epithelial cells and glandular cells. A small number of cases are composed exclusively of spindle epithelial cells or glandular cells.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland papillary and follicular carcinoma
synonyms: thyroid gland papillary and follicular carcinoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A thyroid neoplasm of mixed papillary and follicular arrangement. Its biological behavior and prognosis is the same as that of a papillary adenocarcinoma of the thyroid. (From DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, p1271)

diseases.name: Thyroid gland oncocytic adenoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A thyroid gland adenoma composed of large cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and large nuclei with prominent nucleoli.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma
diseases.group: hereditary disease|immune system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma arising from mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue in the thyroid gland. The vast majority of cases are associated with chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland mucoepidermoid carcinoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A primary, low grade carcinoma of the thyroid gland composed of groups of squamoid and mucous cells, surrounded by fibrous tissue. Prominent cystic structures may be present. The clinical course is usually indolent.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland mucinous carcinoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A thyroid gland carcinoma that is characterized by the presence of clusters of malignant epithelial cells associated with abundant extracellular mucin deposition.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland mixed medullary and follicular cell-derived carcinoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A thyroid gland carcinoma containing a medullary carcinoma component that is immunohistochemically positive for calcitonin, and follicular cell-derived carcinoma component that is immunohistochemically positive for thyroglobulin.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland macrofollicular adenoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A thyroid gland adenoma composed of large size follicles.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland fetal adenoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A thyroid gland adenoma composed of microfollicular structures.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland diffuse sclerosing papillary carcinoma
synonyms: thyroid gland diffuse sclerosing papillary carcinoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A morphologic variant of papillary carcinoma of the thyroid gland that more often affects young patients and commonly metastasizing to the lungs. It is characterized by a diffuse infiltration of the thyroid gland by malignant follicular cells, squamous metaplasia, stromal fibrosis, and lymphocytic infiltration.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland diffuse large b-cell lymphoma
synonyms: thyroid gland diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
primary thyroid gland diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of thyroid gland
diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of thyroid
diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the thyroid gland
diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the thyroid
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A diffuse large B-cell lymphoma primarily involving the thyroid gland.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland cribriform morular carcinoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A thyroid gland carcinoma that is characterized by the presence of cribriform, trabecular, follicular, papillary, and solid growth patterns and squamoid morulae formation.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland atypical follicular adenoma
diseases.group: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A thyroid gland adenoma with increased cellularity and nuclear atypia. There is no capsular or vascular invasion. The clinical course is benign.

diseases.name: Thyroid gland angiosarcoma
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A usually aggressive malignant vascular tumor primarily involving the thyroid gland. It is often associated with longstanding nodular goiter.

diseases.name: Thyroid ectopia
diseases.definition: Thyroid ectopia is a form of thyroid dysgenesis characterized by an ectopic location of the thyroid gland that results in primary congenital hypothyroidism, a permanent thyroid deficiency that is present from birth.

diseases.name: Thyroid dyshormonogenesis 6
synonyms: familial thyroid dyshormonogenesis caused by mutation in DUOX2
diseases.definition: Any familial thyroid dyshormonogenesis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the DUOX2 gene.

diseases.name: Thyroid dyshormonogenesis 5
synonyms: familial thyroid dyshormonogenesis caused by mutation in DUOXA2
diseases.definition: Any familial thyroid dyshormonogenesis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the DUOXA2 gene.

diseases.name: Thyroid dyshormonogenesis 4
synonyms: familial thyroid dyshormonogenesis caused by mutation in IYD
diseases.definition: Any familial thyroid dyshormonogenesis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the IYD gene.

diseases.name: Thyroid dyshormonogenesis 3
synonyms: familial thyroid dyshormonogenesis caused by mutation in TG
diseases.definition: Any familial thyroid dyshormonogenesis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TG gene.

diseases.name: Thyroid dyshormonogenesis 2a
synonyms: familial thyroid dyshormonogenesis caused by mutation in TPO
diseases.definition: Thyroid peroxidase system defect due to presumed mutation(s) in the TPO gene, resulting in decreased activity of thyroid peroxidase.

diseases.name: Thyroid dyshormonogenesis 1
synonyms: iodine accumulation, transport, or trapping defect

diseases.name: Thyroid crisis
diseases.definition: Acute onset of severe, life-threatening hyperthyroidism caused by a sudden release of excessive thyroid hormone.

diseases.group: hereditary disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Any thyroid cancer, nonmedullary in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FOXE1 gene.

Hurthle cell carcinoma of the thyroid

diseases.name: Thyrocerebrorenal syndrome
diseases.definition: Thyrocerebrorenal syndrome is characterized by renal, neurologic, thyroid disease, associated with thrombocytopenia. It has been described in a brother and his sister. Intelligence was normal. It is transmitted as an autosomal recessive trait.

diseases.name: Thymus small cell carcinoma
synonyms: thymic small cell carcinoma neuroendocrine type
small cell carcinoma of the Thymus
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An aggressive, small cell, poorly differentiated thymic neuroendocrine carcinoma, characterized by the presence of a high mitotic rate and numerous apoptotic bodies.

diseases.name: Thymus lipoma
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A well-circumscribed tumor of the thymus composed of islands of normal thymic parenchyma and mature adipose tissue. It is not clear if thymolipoma is a neoplastic or non-neoplastic lesion.

diseases.name: Thymus clear cell carcinoma
synonyms: clear cell carcinoma of the Thymus
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare, usually aggressive, primary thymic carcinoma, characterized by the presence of carcinoma cells with clear cytoplasm.

diseases.name: Thymoma, familial
diseases.group: hereditary disease|immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An instance of thymoma (disease) that is caused by an inherited modification of the individual's genome.

diseases.name: Thymoma type b3
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Also known as well-differentiated thymic carcinoma, atypical thymoma, or epithelial thymoma, this type of thymoma displays morphologic characteristics of a well-differentiated carcinoma. The majority of cases occur in the anterior mediastinum as Masaoka stage II or stage III tumors. It is almost always invasive, it recurs frequently, and metastasizes in approximately 20% of the cases.

diseases.name: Thymoma type b1
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A thymic epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of expanded areas which resemble the normal thymic cortex. The neoplastic epithelial cells are small and scant and there is a dense T-lymphocytic component present. Areas of medullary differentiation with or without Hassall's corpuscles are also present. It may be associated with myasthenia gravis, pure red cell aplasia, and hypogammagl...

diseases.name: Thymoma type b
synonyms: primary thymic epithelial tumour type B
primary thymic epithelial tumor type B
primary thymic epithelial neoplasm type B
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An epithelial neoplasm arising from the thymus. It may be associated with myasthenia gravis, pure red cell aplasia, and hypogammaglobulinemia. It includes thymoma type B1 which is a thymoma of low grade malignant potential, thymoma type B2 which is a thymoma of moderate malignancy, and thymoma type B3 which is also known as well differentiated thymic carcinoma.

diseases.name: Thymoma type ab
synonyms: primary thymic epithelial tumour type AB
primary thymic epithelial tumor type AB
primary thymic epithelial neoplasm type AB
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A thymic epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of a lymphocyte-poor component similar to that seen in type A thymoma and a lymphocyte-rich component which contains neoplastic small polygonal epithelial cells. It may be associated with myasthenia gravis and pure red cell aplasia. The majority of cases occur in the anterior mediastinum as Masaoka stage I tumors. A minority of the case...

diseases.name: Thymoma type a
synonyms: primary thymic epithelial tumour type A
primary thymic epithelial tumor type A
primary thymic epithelial neoplasm type A
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A thymic epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of spindle and/or oval neoplastic epithelial cells. Lymphocytic infiltration is minimal or absent. It may be associated with myasthenia gravis or pure red cell aplasia. The majority of cases occur in the anterior mediastinum as Masaoka stage I tumors. Approximately 20% of the cases occur as stage II or stage III tumors. Type A thymoma g...

diseases.name: Thymoma
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A neoplasm arising from the epithelial cells of the thymus. Although thymomas are usually encapsulated tumors, they may invade the capsule and infiltrate the surrounding tissues or even metastasize to distant anatomic sites. The following morphologic subtypes are currently recognized: type A, type B, type AB, metaplastic, micronodular, microscopic, and sclerosing thymoma. Thymomas type B are fu...

diseases.name: Thymic-renal-anal-lung dysplasia
diseases.definition: This syndrome is characterized by intrauterine growth retardation, renal dysgenesis and a unilobed or absent thymus.

diseases.name: Thymic undifferentiated carcinoma
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare primary thymic carcinoma, characterized by an undifferentiated solid tumor growth, without associated sarcomatoid features.

diseases.name: Thymic sarcomatoid carcinoma
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare, usually aggressive, primary thymic carcinoma, characterized by the presence of tumor cells morphologically resembling soft tissue sarcoma.

diseases.name: Thymic neuroendocrine tumor
synonyms: thymus neuroendocrine tumor, well differentiated, low or intermediate grade
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Thymic endocrine tumor is a rare, malignant, primary thymic neoplasm originating from neuroendocrine cells, presenting as a mass within the anterior mediastinum. Patients typically present with nonspecific symptoms, such as chest pain, cough, shortness of breath, or in some cases, superior vena cava syndrome, although patients could be asymptomatic during the early stages or present with multip...

diseases.name: Thymic neuroendocrine carcinoma
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Thymic neuroendocrine carcinoma is a type of thymic epithelial neoplasm displaying evidence of neuroendocrine differentiation.

diseases.name: Thymic mucoepidermoid carcinoma
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare primary thymic carcinoma, characterized by the presence of squamous cells, intermediate type cells, and mucus-producing cells. Published information on clinical course is limited to single-case reports.

diseases.name: Thymic large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
synonyms: large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of thymus
large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the Thymus
large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of Thymus
large cell carcinoma of the Thymus
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An aggressive, non-small cell, poorly differentiated thymic neuroendocrine carcinoma, characterized by the presence of a high mitotic rate and, almost always, necrosis.

diseases.name: Thymic epithelial neoplasm
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An epithelial neoplasm that affects the thymus gland. This category includes thymomas and carcinomas.

diseases.name: Thymic dysplasia
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder
diseases.definition: The developmental arrest and architectural distortion of the thymus that results in immunodeficiency.

diseases.name: Thymic carcinoma
synonyms: thymic carcinoma excluding well differentiated thymic carcinoma
thymic carcinoma (excluding well differentiated thymic carcinoma)
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Thymic carcinoma (TC) is a type of thymic epithelial neoplasm characterized by a high malignant potential.

diseases.name: Thymic basaloid carcinoma
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare primary thymic carcinoma, characterized by the presence of tumor cell lobules with peripheral palisading, and a basophilic staining pattern. More than half of reported cases were associated with the presence of a multilocular thymic cyst. Metastases to lung and liver have been reported in approximately 30% of cases.

diseases.name: Thymic adenosquamous carcinoma
diseases.group: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare carcinoma that arises from the thymus and is characterized by the presence of glandular and squamous carcinomatous components.

diseases.name: Thygeson superficial punctate keratopathy
diseases.definition: An insidious, chronic and recurrent disorder, characterized by small and elevated oval corneal intraepithelial, whitish-gray opacities, extending to the entire anterior surface of the cornea of both eyes. Corneal lesions show a tendency for the central pupillary area distribution with mild or absent conjunctival inflammation and no association to systemic disease.

diseases.name: Thumb stiffness-brachydactyly-intellectual disability syndrome
diseases.definition: Thumb stiffness-brachydactyly-intellectual disability syndrome is characterized by intellectual deficit, mild dysmorphism, type A brachydactylia, signs of obesity and ankylosis of both thumbs. It has been reported in several females from one family (a girl and her mother, her grandmother and probably also her sister and her great-aunt), as well as in an isolated case.

diseases.name: Thumb deformity-alopecia-pigmentation anomaly syndrome
diseases.definition: A rare, genetic, congenital limb malformation syndrome characterized by short stature, sparse scalp hair, hypoplastic, proximally-placed thumbs, and skin hyperpigmentation with areas of 'raindrop' depigmentation. Presence of a single, upper central incisor has also been reported. There have been no further descriptions in the literature since 1988.

diseases.name: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
diseases.definition: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) is an aggressive and life-threatening form of thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) characterized by profound peripheral thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA) and organ failure of variable severity and is comprised of congenital TTP and acquired TTP.

diseases.name: Thrombotic microangiopathy
diseases.definition: The syndromes of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and variable signs of organ impairment, due to platelet aggregation in the microcirculation.

diseases.name: Thrombophlebitis migrans
diseases.definition: A thrombophlebitis that is characterized by repeated occurrences of thrombophlebitis in different locations.

diseases.name: Thrombophlebitis
synonyms: thrombophlebitis of superficial veins of lower extremity
thrombophlebitis of a superficial leg vein
phlebitis and thrombophlebitis of superficial vessels of lower extremities
diseases.definition: Inflammation of the veins associated with the presence of a thrombus.

diseases.name: Thrombophilia, familial, due to decreased release of tissue plasminogen activator
synonyms: thrombophilia, familial, due to decreased release of tissue plasminogen activator
thrombophilia, familial, due to decreased release of PLAT
hyperfibrinolysis, familial, due to increased release of plat

diseases.name: Thrombophilia, x-linked, due to factor 9 defect
synonyms: thrombophilia, X-linked, due to factor IX defect
thrombophilia, X-linked, due to factor 9 defect
thrombophilia 8, X-linked, due to factor IX defect, X-linked recessive
deep venous thrombosis, protection against, X-linked recessive
diseases.definition: A hemostatic disorder characterized by a tendency to thrombosis that has X-linked recessive inheritance, and can be caused by a gain-of-function mutation in the gene encoding factor IX (F9).

diseases.name: Thrombophilia, x-linked, due to factor 8 defect
Thrombophilia due to thrombin defect

autosomal dominant hereditary thrombophilia due to congenital protein S deficiency

thrombophilia 3 due to protein C deficiency, autosomal recessive

diseases.name: Thrombophilia due to activated protein c resistance
synonyms: thrombophilia due to activated protein C resistance
thrombophilia 2 due to activated protein C resistance
diseases.definition: A hemostatic disorder characterized by a poor anticoagulant response to activated protein C (APC). The activated form of Factor V (Factor Va) is more slowly degraded by activated protein C. Factor V Leiden mutation (R506Q) is the most common cause of APC resistance.

diseases.name: Thrombocytopenia-absent radius syndrome
synonyms: 1q21.1 susceptibility locus for Thrombocytopenia-Absent Radius (TAR) syndrome
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease|hematologic disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Thrombocytopenia-absent radius (TAR) syndrome is a very rare congenital malformation syndrome characterized by bilateral radial aplasia and thrombocytopenia.

diseases.name: Thrombocytopenia, x-linked, with or without dyserythropoietic anemia
synonyms: thrombocytopenia, X-linked, with or without dyserythropoietic anemia, X-linked recessive
thrombocytopenia, X-linked, with or without dyserythropoietic anemia
X-linked thrombocytopenia, with or without dyserythropoietic Anemia
X-linked thrombocytopenia, with or without dyserythropoietic Anaemia
diseases.definition: An X-linked condition caused by mutation(s) in the GATA1 gene, encoding erythroid transcription factor. It is characterized by thrombocytopenia, as well as abnormal platelet function and morphology. Dyserythropoietic anemia of variable severity may also be present.

diseases.name: Thrombocytopenia with elevated serum iga and renal disease
synonyms: thrombocytopenia with elevated serum IgA and renal disease

diseases.name: Thrombocytopenia with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia
synonyms: X-linked congenital dyserythropoietic anemia with thrombocytopenia
X-linked congenital dyserythropoietic anaemia with thrombocytopenia
diseases.definition: Thrombocytopenia with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia (CDA) is a rare hematological disorder, seen almost exclusively in males, characterized by moderate to severe thrombocytopenia with hemorrhages with or without the presence of mild to severe anemia.

diseases.name: Thrombocytopenia due to immune destruction
diseases.definition: A general class of thrombocytopenia due to immune destruction of platelets. It includes idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, as well as immune destruction-related thrombocytopenias due to other reasons (e.g., AIDS, transfusion, lupus erythematosus).

diseases.name: Thrombocytopenia 6
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|connective tissue disorder|immune system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Thrombocytopenia 5
synonyms: thrombocytopenia caused by mutation in ETV6
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Any thrombocytopenia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ETV6 gene.

diseases.name: Thrombocytopenia 4
synonyms: thrombocytopenia caused by mutation in CYCS
diseases.definition: Any thrombocytopenia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the CYCS gene.

diseases.name: Thrombocytopenia 2
diseases.definition: An autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutation(s) in the ANKRD26 gene, encoding ANKRD26 protein. Additionally, in one family, a mutation(s) has been identified in the MASTL gene, encoding serine/threonine-protein kinase greatwall. The condition is characterized by mild to moderate bruisability.

diseases.name: Thrombocytopenia 11 with multiple congenital anomalies and dysmorphic facies
Thrombocythemia 3
synonyms: familial thrombocytosis caused by mutation in JAK2
diseases.definition: Familial thrombocytosis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the JAK2 gene.

diseases.name: Thrombocythemia 2
synonyms: familial thrombocytosis caused by mutation in MPL
diseases.definition: Familial thrombocytosis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the MPL gene.

diseases.name: Thromboangiitis obliterans
diseases.definition: A rare inflammatory non-necrotizing vascular disease affecting the small- and medium-sized arteries and veins of the upper and lower extremities characterized by endarteritis and vaso-occlusion due to occlusive thrombus development. The development and progression of the disease is consistently associated with exposure to tobacco.

diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Thoracolaryngopelvic dysplasia

diseases.definition: A short-rib dysplasia characterized by thoracic dystrophy, laryngeal stenosis and a small pelvis.

diseases.name: Thoraco-abdominal enteric duplication
diseases.definition: Thoraco-abdominal enteric duplication is a rare, syndromic intestinal malformation characterized by single or multiple smooth-walled, often tubular, cystic lesions, which on occasion contain ectopic gastric mucosa, located in the thorax (usually in the posterior mediastinum and to the right of the midline) and in the abdomen. Infants usually present with respiratory distress and older patients ...

diseases.name: Thoracic spinal canal and spinal cord meningioma
synonyms: meningioma of thoracic spinal canal and spinal cord
meningioma of the thoracic spinal canal and spinal cord
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A meningioma that arises from the meninges of the thoracic region of the spinal cord.

diseases.name: Thoracic outlet syndrome
diseases.definition: A syndrome resulting from the compression of the blood vessels or nerves in the space between the clavicle and first rib (thoracic outlet). It is caused by car accident injuries or repetitive job or sport-related injuries. Signs and symptoms include pain in the shoulders and neck, numbness in the fingers, and weakening grip.

diseases.name: Thoracic disk degenerative disorder

thoracic region of vertebral column intervertebral disc degenerative disorder
intervertebral disk degenerative disorder of thoracic region of vertebral column
intervertebral disc degenerative disorder of thoracic region of vertebral column
diseases.definition: Any degenerative disorder affecting one or more vertebral disks of the thoracic spine.

diseases.name: Thoracic cancer
synonyms: malignant thoracic segment of trunk neoplasm
malignant neoplasm of thoracic segment of trunk
cancer of thoracic segment of trunk
diseases.definition: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm affecting the tissues of the thorax.

diseases.name: Thoracic aortic aneurysm
diseases.definition: An aneurysm formed in the wall of the proximal portion of the descending aorta proceeding from the arch of the aorta.

diseases.name: Third-degree atrioventricular block
diseases.definition: A disorder characterized by an electrocardiographic finding of complete failure of atrial electrical impulse conduction to the ventricles. This is manifested on the ECG by disassociation of atrial and ventricular rhythms. The atrial rate must be faster than the ventricular rate. (CDISC)

diseases.group: disorder of development or morphogenesis|otorhinolaryngologic disease

diseases.name: Thiopurine immunosuppressant-induced pancreatitis
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: Pancreatits that is the result of treatment with thiopurine immunosuppressants such as azathioprine or mercaptopurine.

diseases.name: Thiopurine s-methyltransferase deficiency
synonyms: rare inborn error of thiopurine S-methyltransferase activity
inborn error of thiopurine S-methyltransferase activity
diseases.definition: An inherited metabolic disease that is has its basis in the disruption of thiopurine S-methyltransferase activity.

diseases.name: Thinking seizures
diseases.definition: Thinking seizures is a rare neurologic disease characterized by seizures induced by specific cognitive tasks, such as calculation or solving arithmetic problems (e.g Sudoku puzzle), playing thinking games (e.g. Rubik's cube, chess, cards), thinking, making decisions and abstract reasoning. Idiopathic generalized seizures are mainly involved, but partial epilepsies may, in rare cases, be observed.

diseases.name: Thickened earlobes-conductive deafness syndrome
diseases.definition: Thickened earlobes-conductive deafness syndrome is characterized by microtia with thickened ear lobes, micrognathia and conductive hearing loss due to congenital ossicular anomalies. It has been described in two families. The mode of inheritance is autosomal dominant.

diseases.name: Thickened earlobes with conductive deafness from incus-stapes abnormalities
synonyms: thickened earlobes with conductive deafness from incus-stapes abnormalities

diseases.name: Thiamine-responsive megaloblastic anemia syndrome
synonyms: thiamine-responsive megaloblastic anemia with diabetes mellitus and sensorineural deafness
thiamine-responsive megaloblastic anaemia with diabetes mellitus and sensorineural deafness
diseases.definition: Thiamine-responsive megaloblastic anemia (TRMA) is characterized by a triad of megaloblastic anemia, non-type I diabetes mellitus, and sensorineural deafness.

diseases.name: Thiamine-responsive maple syrup urine disease
diseases.definition: Thiamine-responsive maple syrup urine disease (thiamine-responsive MSUD) is a less severe variant of MSUD that manifests with a phenotype similar to intermediate MSUD but that responds positively to treatment with thiamine.

diseases.name: Therapy-related myeloid neoplasm
synonyms: therapy-related acute myeloid leukemia and myelodysplastic syndrome
therapy-related acute myeloid leukaemia and myelodysplastic syndrome
acute myeloid Leukaemias and myelodysplastic syndromes, therapy-related
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|immune system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Acute myeloid leukemias, myelodysplastic syndromes, and myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasms arising as a result of the mutagenic effect of chemotherapy agents and/or radiation that are used for the treatment of neoplastic or non-neoplastic disorders.

diseases.name: Thelaziasis
diseases.definition: A disease caused by infection with Thelazia.

diseases.name: Theileriasis
diseases.definition: Infection of cattle, sheep, or goats with protozoa of the genus theileria. This infection results in an acute or chronic febrile condition.

diseases.name: Theca steroid-producing cell malignant tumor of ovary, not further specified
synonyms: theca (steroid-producing) cell cancer, not further specified
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Malignant steroid cell tumor of the ovary, not otherwise specified is a rare malignant sex cord stromal tumor of ovary of unknown histological lineage, occurring in adult women, characterized, in most cases, by manifestations of androgen excess (hirsutism, hair loss, amenorrhea, or oligomenorrhea) and, occasionally, Cushing syndrome.

diseases.name: Thanatophoric dysplasia, glasgow variant
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Thanatophoric dysplasia type 2
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Thanatophoric dysplasia characterized by a cloverleaf-like skull and straight femurs.

diseases.name: Thanatophoric dysplasia type 1
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Thanatophoric dysplasia type 1 (TD1) is a form of TD characterized by short, bowed femurs, micromelia, narrow thorax, and brachydactyly.

diseases.name: Thanatophoric dysplasia
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: A primary bone dysplasia with micromelia characterized by macrocephaly, narrow thorax, and distinctive facial features. It includes TD, type 1 (TD1) and TD, type 2 (TD2), that can be differentiated from each other by femur and skull shape.

diseases.name: Thalidomide embryopathy
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|syndromic disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: A group of anomalies presented in infants as a result of in utero exposure (between 20-36 days after fertilization) to thalidomide, a sedative used in treatment of a range of conditions, including morning sickness, leprosy and multiple myeloma (see these terms). Thalidomine embryopathy is characterized by phocomelia, amelia, forelimb and hand plate anomalies (absence of humerus and/or forearm, ...

diseases.name: Thalassemia minor
diseases.definition: The inheritance of only one mutated beta-globin allele (beta+ or beta0).

diseases.name: Tetrasomy x
diseases.group: hereditary disease|reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|chromosomal disorder
diseases.definition: Tetrasomy X is a sex chromosome anomaly caused by the presence of two extra X chromosomes in females (48,XXXX instead of 46,XX).

diseases.name: Tetrasomy 9p
diseases.definition: Tetrasomy 9p is a rare autosomal anomaly characterized by pre- and postnatal growth retardation, psychomotor delay, mild to moderate intellectual disability, hypotonia, microcephaly, dysmorphic features (ocular hypertelorism, low-set, malformed ears, bulbous/beaked nose, microretrognathia, enophthalmos/micropthalmia, epicanthus, strabismus), cleft lip/palate, skeletal abnormalities (hypoplastic...

diseases.name: Tetrasomy 5p
diseases.definition: Tetrasomy 5p is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome with variable phenotype principally characterized by developmental delay, growth retardation/short stature, hypotonia, seizures, venriculomegaly, hand and foot anomalies (e.g. clinodactyly, overlapping toes) and mosaic pigmentary skin changes. Patients may also present minor dysmorphic craniofacial features (incl. macrocephaly, upslanting palp...

diseases.name: Tetrasomy 21
diseases.definition: Tetrasomy 21 is an extremely rare autosomal anomaly resulting from the presence of 4 copies of chromosome 21, characterized by features of trisomy 21 including developmental delay/intellectual disability, muscular hypotonia, short neck with redundant skin, brachycephaly, microcephaly, flat face, epicanthus, upslanted palpebral fissures, small ears, protruding tongue, single transverse palmar cr...

diseases.name: Tetrasomy 18p
diseases.definition: Tetrasomy 18p is a very rare structural chromosomal anomaly affecting multiple body systems and characterized clinically by craniofacial abnormalities, delayed development, cognitive impairment, changes in muscle tone, distinctive facial features, and rarely renal malformations.

diseases.name: Tetrasomy 12p
diseases.group: syndromic disease|chromosomal disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Pallister-Killian syndrome (PKS) is a rare multiple congenital anomaly/intellectual deficit syndrome caused by mosaic tissue-limited tetrasomy for chromosome 12p.

diseases.name: Tetraploidy syndrome
diseases.definition: The presence of four sets of chromosomes. It is associated with abnormalities, multiple; and miscarrages.

diseases.name: Tetramelic monodactyly
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Tetramelic monodactyly is a rare, genetic, congenital limb malformation disorder characterized by the presence of a single digit on all four extremities. Malformation is typically isolated however, aplastic and hypoplastic defects in the remaining skeletal parts of hands and feet have been reported. There have been no further descriptions in the literature since 1992.

diseases.name: Tetralogy of fallot syndrome, autosomal recessive
synonyms: tetralogy of fallot syndrome, autosomal recessive

diseases.name: Tetralogy of fallot
synonyms: ventricular septal defect with pulmonary stenosis or atresia, dextraposition of aorta, and hypertrophy of right ventricle
diseases.group: hereditary disease|cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Tetralogy of Fallot is a congenital cardiac malformation that consists of an interventricular communication, also known as a ventricular septal defect, obstruction of the right ventricular outflow tract, override of the ventricular septum by the aortic root, and right ventricular hypertrophy.

diseases.name: Tetrahydrobiopterin-responsive hyperphenylalaninemia/phenylketonuria
diseases.definition: Tetrahydrobiopterin-responsive hyperphenylalaninemia/ phenylketonuria (BH4-responsive hyperphenylalaninemia/ phenylketonuria) is a form of phenylketonuria (PKU), an inborn error of amino acid metabolism, characterized by mild to moderate symptoms of PKU including impaired cognitive function, seizures, and behavioral and developmental disorders, and a marked reduction and normalization of elevat...

diseases.name: Tetrahydrobiopterin (bh4)-deficient hyperphenylalaninemia
diseases.definition: An amino acid metabolic disorder that are characterized phenotypically by hyperphenylalaninemia, depletion of the neurotransmitters dopamine and serotonin, and progressive cognitive and motor deficits and that has material basis in autosomal recessive mutations in the genes encoding enzymes involved in the synthesis or regeneration of BH4.

diseases.name: Tetragametic chimerism
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Tetragametic chimerism is a rare, sex chromosome disorder of sex development characterized by the two different haploid sets of maternal and paternal chromosomes and variable phenotype - from normal male or female genitalia, to different degrees of ambiguous genitalia, and often infertility. Also, in the cases of monochorionic dizygotic twins, it can be confined to blood of both twins.

diseases.name: Tetraamelia-multiple malformations syndrome
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Tetraamelia - multiple malformations is an extremely rare mostly lethal congenital disorder characterized by absence of all four limbs and frequent associated major malformations involving the head, face, eyes, skeleton, heart, lungs, anus, urogenital, and central nervous systems. The syndrome has been described in fewer than 20 patients mainly of middle Eastern descent.

diseases.name: Tetraamelia with ectodermal dysplasia and lacrimal duct abnormalities

diseases.name: Tetraamelia syndrome 2

diseases.name: Tetra-amelia

diseases.name: Tethered spinal cord syndrome
diseases.definition: A progressive neurological disorder characterized by the limitation of movement of the spinal cord within the spine. It is caused by the presence of congenital or acquired tissue attachments in the spinal cord. Signs and symptoms include low back pain, scoliosis, weakness in the legs, and incontinence.

diseases.name: Tetanus neonatorum
diseases.definition: A syndrome of generalized rigidity with muscle spasms and seizures in the neonatal period resulting from Clostridium tetani toxin production.

diseases.name: Tetanus
synonyms: Clostridium tetani infectious disease of the nervous system
Clostridium tetani caused infectious disease of the nervous system
diseases.definition: A serious infectious disorder that follows wound contamination by the Gram-positive bacterium Clostridium tetani. The bacteria produce a neurotoxin called tetanospasmin, which causes muscle spasm in the jaw and other anatomic sites.

diseases.name: Tetanic cataract
diseases.definition: A cataract resulting from hypocalcemia.

diseases.name: Testis rhabdomyosarcoma
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A malignant mesenchymal tumor with skeletal muscle differentiation affecting the testis.

diseases.name: Testis refractory cancer
synonyms: refractory malignant testicular germ cell tumour
refractory malignant testicular germ cell tumor
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Malignant testicular germ cell tumor that is resistant to treatment.

diseases.name: Testis polyembryoma
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare malignant germ cell tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of embryoid bodies.

diseases.name: Testicular yolk sac tumor, solid pattern
synonyms: testicular yolk sac tumor, solid pattern
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A yolk sac tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of aggregates of polygonal malignant cells with clear cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli.

diseases.name: Testicular yolk sac tumor, papillary pattern
synonyms: testicular yolk sac tumor, papillary pattern
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A yolk sac tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of numerous papillary structures that are lined by cells with prominent nucleoli.

diseases.name: Testicular yolk sac tumor, myxomatous pattern
synonyms: testicular yolk sac tumor, myxomatous pattern
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A yolk sac tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of myxomatous tissue that contains collections of malignant cells with prominent nucleoli.

diseases.name: Testicular yolk sac tumor, macrocystic pattern
synonyms: testicular yolk sac tumor, macrocystic pattern
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A yolk sac tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of collections of thin-walled spaces.

diseases.name: Testicular yolk sac tumor, hepatoid pattern
synonyms: testicular yolk sac tumor, hepatoid pattern
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A yolk sac tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of hepatoid cells collections.

diseases.name: Testicular yolk sac tumor, glandular-alveolar pattern
synonyms: testicular yolk sac tumor, glandular-alveolar pattern
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A yolk sac tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of gland-like spaces, irregular alveoli, and tubular structures.

diseases.name: Testicular yolk sac tumor, endodermal sinus pattern
synonyms: testicular yolk sac tumor, endodermal sinus pattern
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A yolk sac tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of connective tissue stalks that contain a blood vessel and are lined by cells with clear cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli.

diseases.name: Testicular thecoma
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare benign tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of lipid-rich neoplastic spindle cells.

diseases.name: Testicular teratoma
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Testicular sex cord-stromal neoplasm
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A benign or malignant tumor that arises from the testis. It is composed of granulosa cells, Leydig cells, Sertoli cells, and fibroblasts. Each of these cell types may constitute the only cellular component that is present in the tumor or it may be mixed with other cell types in various combinations. The prognosis can not always be predicted on histologic grounds alone. Approximately, ten percen...

diseases.name: Testicular sex cord-stromal benign neoplasm
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A sex cord-stromal benign neoplasm that arises from the testis.

diseases.name: Testicular seminoma
synonyms: seminomatous germ cell tumour of testis
seminomatous germ cell tumor of testis
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A malignant germ cell tumor arising from the testis. It is believed that it is derived from the sexually undifferentiated embryonic gonad. Treatment with radiotherapy is highly successful when the tumor is diagnosed in localized stages, which represents the majority of presentations of seminoma.

diseases.name: Testicular non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
synonyms: testicular non seminomatous germ cell tumour
testicular non seminomatous germ cell tumor
non-seminomatous germ cell tumour of testis
non-seminomatous germ cell tumor of testis
non-dysgerminomatous germ cell tumour of testis
non-dysgerminomatous germ cell tumor of testis
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A testicular germ cell tumor characterized by the absence of a seminomatous component. It includes embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor, choriocarcinoma, teratoma, and mixed forms.

diseases.name: Testicular monophasic choriocarcinoma
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A choriocarcinoma that arises from the testis and is characterized by the predominance of cytotrophoblastic and intermediate trophoblastic cells. Syncytiotrophoblastic cells are absent or not prominent.

diseases.name: Testicular lymphoma
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A lymphoma that arises from the testis and is not associated with lymphoma in another anatomic site.

diseases.name: Testicular leukemia
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A myeloid or more commonly lymphoid leukemia (acute or chronic) affecting the testis. Microscopically, there is interstitial infiltration of the testis by leukemic cells. Acute lymphoblastic leukemia with testicular involvement is not uncommon in boys. Sometimes (up to 10% of the cases), testicular involvement may be the initial manifestation of relapsed acute lymphoblastic leukemia. --03

diseases.name: Testicular infarct
diseases.definition: Ischemic necrosis of the testis usually caused by torsion of the spermatic cord, trauma, or severe epididymo-orchitis.

diseases.name: Testicular gonadoblastoma
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A testicular mixed germ cell-sex cord-stromal tumor. It is usually associated with mixed gonadal dysgenesis and ambiguous genitalia. It is characterized by the presence of nests of large neoplastic germ cells and immature cells that resemble Sertoli cells.

synonyms: germ cell tumour of the testis
germ cell tumor of the testis
germ cell neoplasm of the testis
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A germ cell tumor arising from the testis. Representative examples include teratoma, seminoma, embryonal carcinoma, and yolk sac tumor.

diseases.name: Testicular fibrothecoma
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare testicular sex cord-stromal neoplasm characterized by mixed features of both fibroma and thecoma.

diseases.name: Testicular fibroma
diseases.group: connective tissue disorder|reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A benign neoplasm that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of fusiform cells and collagenization.

diseases.name: Testicular dysgenesis syndrome
diseases.definition: A syndrome comprising testicular germ cell cancer, cryptorchidism and some cases of hypospadias and male infertility with impaired development of the testis.

diseases.name: Testicular anomalies with or without congenital heart disease

diseases.name: Testicular brenner tumor
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An uncommon usually benign neoplasm that arises from the testis. It is characterized by the presence of cysts lined by transitional cells and solid nests of transitional cells in a spindle cell stroma.

diseases.name: Tertiary hyperparathyroidism
diseases.definition: An overproduction of parathyroid hormone that is autonomous and often associated with chronic secondary hyperparathyroidism.

diseases.name: Terminal transverse defects of arm
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Terminal osseous dysplasia-pigmentary defects syndrome
diseases.definition: A syndrome characterized by malformation of the hands and feet, pigmentary skin lesions on the face and scalp and digital fibromatosis.

diseases.name: Terminal myelocystocele
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: A rare closed spinal dysraphism characterized by a myelocystocele at the termination of the spinal cord. It may be an isolated anomaly or be associated with other defects, including sacral agenesis, anorectal and genitourinary anomalies. The conus is not identifiable. The myelocystocele sac may have a significant lipomatous component (terminal lipomyelocystocele).

diseases.name: Terminal extramedullary conus spinal cord lipoma
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|connective tissue disorder|nervous system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare form of extramedullary conus region spinal cord lipoma characterized by its location, extending from the poorly delineated tip of the conus.

diseases.group: nervous system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Teratocarcinoma
diseases.definition: A germ cell tumor characterized by the presence of an embryonal carcinoma component and a teratoma component.

The tumor is slow-growing, usually developing over several years. Clinical presentation inclu...
