diseases.name: Breast synovial sarcoma
diseases.definition: A synovial sarcoma (disease) that involves the breast.

diseases.name: Breast rhabdomyosarcoma
diseases.definition: A malignant mesenchymal tumor with skeletal muscle differentiation affecting the breast.

diseases.name: Breast pericanalicular fibroadenoma
diseases.definition: A morphologic variant of breast fibroadenoma without clinical significance. It is characterized by circumferential proliferation of stromal cells around the ducts. This results in the formation of rounded ductal-epithelial structures.

diseases.name: Breast myofibroblastoma
diseases.group: breast disorder|connective tissue disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A myofibroblastoma occurring in the breast of both women and men. It presents as a slowly growing mass.

diseases.name: Breast mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|hereditary disease|immune system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma of mucosa associated lymphoid tissue that arises from the breast as a primary tumor.

diseases.name: Breast mucinous cystadenocarcinoma
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|breast disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An invasive breast adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of tall columnar neoplastic cells that contain intracytoplasmic mucin. Grossly, cystic changes are identified.

diseases.name: Breast malignant eccrine spiradenoma
synonyms: malignant eccrine spiradenoma of the breast
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|breast disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare tumor characterized by malignant transformation of an eccrine spiradenoma of the breast.

diseases.name: Breast liposarcoma
diseases.group: breast disorder|connective tissue disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A malignant adipose tissue neoplasm of the breast.

diseases.name: Breast lipoma
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|breast disorder|connective tissue disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A benign, mesenchymal neoplasm that arises from the breast. It is surrounded by a thin capsule and composed of mature adipose tissue cells. Atypia is absent.

diseases.name: Breast leiomyosarcoma
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|breast disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An aggressive malignant smooth muscle neoplasm, arising from the breast. It is characterized by a proliferation of neoplastic spindle cells.

diseases.name: Breast leiomyoma
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|breast disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A well-circumscribed benign smooth muscle neoplasm arising from the breast. It is characterized by the presence of spindle cells with cigar-shaped nuclei, interlacing fascicles, and a whorled pattern.

diseases.name: Breast large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
synonyms: large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of breast
diseases.group: breast disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma that arises from the breast. It is characterized by the presence of large neuroendocrine cells and high mitotic activity.

diseases.name: Breast intracanalicular fibroadenoma
diseases.definition: A morphologic variant of breast fibroadenoma without clinical significance. It is characterized by distortion and compression of the ducts by proliferating stromal cells.

diseases.name: Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma
Breast implant illness
diseases.definition: A syndrome that is characterized by fatigue, problems with memory or concentration, joint and muscle pain, hair loss, weight changes and anxiety/depression. This syndrome may be related to breast implants

diseases.name: Breast hemangiopericytoma
diseases.definition: A hemangiopericytoma arising from the breast.

diseases.name: Breast granular cell tumor
diseases.group: breast disorder|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A usually benign neoplasm that arises from the breast. It presents as a single, firm, and painless mass. It is characterized by the presence of neoplastic cells with eosinophilic granular cytoplasm.

diseases.name: Breast giant fibroadenoma
diseases.definition: A breast fibroadenoma characterized by a very large size. This term has also been used as a synonym for juvenile fibroadenoma by some authors. The latter is characterized by epithelial hyperplasia and an increased stromal cellularity.

diseases.name: Breast fibrosis
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|breast disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Breast fibrocystic change characterized by the prominence of fibrotic changes in the parenchyma.

diseases.name: Breast fibrosarcoma
diseases.group: breast disorder|connective tissue disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A usually aggressive malignant neoplasm arising from the breast. It is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and collagenous stroma formation in a herringbone growth pattern.

diseases.name: Breast fibrocystic disease
diseases.definition: Fibrosis associated with cyst formation in the breast parenchyma.

diseases.name: Breast extraskeletal osteosarcoma
diseases.definition: An osteosarcoma arising from the breast tissue.

diseases.name: Breast epithelioid hemangioma
diseases.group: breast disorder|cardiovascular disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A hemangioma characterized by the presence of epithelioid endothelial cells, arising from the breast.

diseases.name: Breast ductal adenoma
diseases.definition: A benign, well circumscribed neoplasm that is located within the lumen of a duct in the breast parenchyma. It is characterized by the presence of glandular structures at the periphery and fibrous tissue at the center of the tumor.

diseases.name: Breast diffuse large b-cell lymphoma
synonyms: diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of breast
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|breast disorder|immune system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that arises from the breast. It is the most common type of primary breast lymphoma.

diseases.name: Breast cystic hypersecretory carcinoma
synonyms: cystic hypersecretory duct carcinoma of the breast
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|breast disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Breast columnar cell mucinous carcinoma
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|breast disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An invasive breast adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of tall columnar neoplastic cells that contain intracytoplasmic mucin. Grossly, cystic changes are not identified.

diseases.name: Breast capillary hemangioma
diseases.group: breast disorder|cardiovascular disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A capillary hemangioma arising from the breast.

apocrine carcinoma in situ of breast
diseases.definition: A ductal breast carcinoma in situ, characterized by the presence of neoplastic epithelial cells with apocrine differentiation.

diseases.name: Breast apocrine carcinoma
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|breast disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An adenocarcinoma of the breast characterized by the presence of two intermingled cellular components: cells with abundant granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm, and cells with abundant cytoplasm containing fine empty vacuoles.

diseases.name: Breast apocrine adenoma
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|breast disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare, benign and well circumscribed neoplasm that arises from the breast. It is characterized by the proliferation of epithelial cells with extensive apocrine metaplasia.

diseases.name: Breast angiosarcoma
diseases.group: breast disorder|cardiovascular disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A malignant vascular neoplasm arising from the breast.

diseases.name: Breast angiomatosis
diseases.definition: A benign diffuse vascular proliferation in the breast. It is characterized by the formation of capillary-sized and cavernous vascular spaces.

diseases.name: Breast adenomyoepithelial adenosis
diseases.definition: An uncommon variant of breast adenosis characterized by the presence of irregularly shaped glands, epithelial cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm, and prominent myopepithelial cells. Mild atypia may be present.

diseases.name: Breast abscess

diseases.definition: Bilateral renal agenesis is the most profound form of renal agenesis, characterized by complete absence of kidney development, absent ureters and subsequent absence of fetal renal function resulting in Potter sequence with pulmonary hypoplasia related to oligohydramnios, which is fatal shortly after birth.

diseases.name: Bilateral polymicrogyria
diseases.definition: Bilateral polymicrogyria is a rare cerebral malformation due to abnormal neuronal migration defined as a cerebral cortex with many excessively small convolutions. It presents with developmental delay, intellectual disability, seizures and various neurological impairments and may be isolated or comprise a clinical feature of many genetic syndromes. It may also be associated with perinatal cytome...

diseases.name: Bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidney
diseases.group: urinary system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK) is a lethal form of multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK), a congenital anomaly of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT), in which both kidneys are large, distended by non-communicating multiple cysts and non-functional.

diseases.name: Bilateral microtia-deafness-cleft palate syndrome
synonyms: microtia, hearing impairment, and cleft palate (AR)
microtia with or without hearing impairment (AD)
diseases.definition: This syndrome is characterized by the association of bilateral microtia with severe to profound hearing impairment, and cleft palate.

diseases.name: Bilateral meningioma of optic nerve
synonyms: bilateral meningioma of the optic nerve
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Meningiomas that affects both optic nerves.

diseases.name: Bilateral massive adrenal hemorrhage
diseases.definition: A serious adrenal gland disorder characterized by acute bleeding into both adrenal glands. It is associated with illnesses such as severe sepsis, congestive heart failure, autoimmune etiologies such as antiphospholipid syndrome, the use of anticoagulants; especially in the setting of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, as well as severe physical stress such as trauma and surgery.

diseases.name: Bilateral generalized polymicrogyria
synonyms: microcephaly, short stature, and polymicrogyria with seizures
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|syndromic disease|hereditary disease|nervous system disorder
diseases.definition: Bilateral generalized polymicrogyria is a rare neurological disorder that affects the cerebral cortex (the outer surface of the brain). This is the most widespread form of polymicrogyria and typically affects the entire surface of the brain. Signs and symptoms include severe intellectual disability, problems with movement, and seizures that are difficult or impossible to treat. While the exact ...

diseases.name: Bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria
diseases.definition: A descriptive term reflecting increased gyral folding in the frontoparietal regions as determined by magnetic resonance imaging. It has subsequently been shown to represent a cobblestone malformation on histopathology. BFPP typically presents with hypotonia, developmental delay, moderate to severe intellectual disability, pyramidal signs, epileptic seizures, non-progressive cerebellar ataxia, d...

diseases.name: Bilateral frontal polymicrogyria
diseases.definition: Bilateral frontal polymicrogyria is one of the rarest subtypes of polymicrogyria. It is a symmetric and bilateral form (in both brain hemispheres) that only involves the frontal lobes without including the area located behind the Sylvius fissure or the area located behind the Rolando sulcus. Some researchers classify the condition into two different forms: bilateral frontal polymicrogyriaand th...

Bilateral acute depigmentation of the iris
diseases.group: hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis|disorder of visual system
diseases.definition: Bilateral acute depigmentation of the iris (BADI) is characterized by acute onset of bilateral iris depigmentation, pigment dispersion in the anterior chamber, and heavy pigment deposition in the anterior chamber angle. Patients typically present with acute and usually severe photophobia, blurred vision, red eye, and ocular discomfort or pain with a usually self-limiting clinical course. Cases ...

diseases.name: Bifid uvula
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Bifid uvula is a fissure type embryopathy affecting the uvula at the back of the soft palate.

diseases.name: Bifid nose, autosomal recessive
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis|otorhinolaryngologic disease
diseases.definition: Autosomal recessive form of bifid nose.

diseases.name: Bifid nose, autosomal dominant

diseases.name: Bifid nose
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis|otorhinolaryngologic disease
diseases.definition: Bifid nose is a rare congenital malformation of presumed autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance characterized by clefting of the nose ranging from a minimally noticeable groove in the columella to complete clefting of the underlying bones and cartilage (resulting in two half noses) with a usually adequate airway. Bifid nose may be seen in frontonasal dysplasia while other malformations suc...

diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|disorder of visual system

diseases.name: Beta-ureidopropionase deficiency
diseases.definition: Beta-ureidopropionase deficiency is a very rare pyrimidine metabolism disorder described in fewer than 10 patients to date with an extremely wide clinical picture ranging from asymptomatic cases to neurological (epilepsy, autism) and developmental disorders (urogenital, colorectal).

diseases.name: Beta-thalassemia-x-linked thrombocytopenia syndrome
synonyms: thrombocytopenia with beta-thalassemia, X-linked, X-linked recessive
diseases.definition: Beta-thalassemia - X-linked thrombocytopenia is a form of beta-thalassemia characterized by splenomegaly and petechiae, moderate thrombocytopenia, prolonged bleeding time due to platelet dysfunction, reticulocytosis and mild beta-thalassemia.

diseases.name: Beta-thalassemia major
diseases.definition: Beta-thalassemia (BT) major is a severe early-onset form of BT characterized by severe anemia requiring regular red blood cell transfusions.

diseases.name: Beta-thalassemia intermedia
diseases.definition: Beta-thalassemia (BT) intermedia is a form of BT characterized by mild to moderate anemia which does not or only occasionally requires transfusion.

diseases.name: Beta-thalassemia hbb/lcrb
diseases.definition: Abnormal clinical manifestations of beta thalassemia that are as a result of the underlying genotype.

diseases.name: Beta-mannosidosis
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|metabolic disease|nervous system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Beta-mannosidosis is a very rare lysosomal storage disease characterized by developmental delay of varying severity and hearing loss, but that can manifest a wide phenotypic heterogeneity.

diseases.name: Beta-ketothiolase deficiency
diseases.definition: Beta-ketothiolase (T2) deficiency is a rare organic aciduria affecting ketone body metabolism and the catabolism of isoleucine and characterized by intermittent ketoacidotic episodes associated with vomiting, dyspnea, tachypnoea, hypotonia, lethargy and coma, with an onset during infancy or toddlerhood and usually ceasing by adolescence.

diseases.name: Beta thalassemia
diseases.definition: Beta-thalassemia (BT) is characterized by deficiency (Beta+) or absence (Beta0) of synthesis of the beta globin chains of hemoglobin (Hb).

diseases.name: Berry aneurysm, cirrhosis, pulmonary emphysema, and cerebral calcification
synonyms: berry aneurysm, cirrhosis, pulmonary emphysema, and cerebral calcification

diseases.name: Beriberi
diseases.definition: Beriberi is a condition that occurs in people who are deficient in thiamine (vitamin B1). There are two major types of beriberi: wet beriberi which affects the cardiovascular system and dry beriberi which affects the nervous system. People with wet beriberi may experience increased heart rate, shortness of breath, and swelling of the lower legs. Signs and symptoms of dry beriberi include diffic...

diseases.name: Benign vaginal neoplasm
synonyms: vagina female reproductive organ benign neoplasm
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the vagina. Representative examples include squamous papilloma and melanocytic nevus.

diseases.name: Benign vaginal mixed tumor
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A non-metastasizing, well circumscribed neoplasm that arises from the vagina and is characterized by the presence of a predominant benign mesenchymal component and benign glandular or squamous epithelial cells.

diseases.name: Benign teratoma
diseases.definition: A germ cell benign neoplasm that derives from mature tissue elements or a limited amount of immature tissue elements.

diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|digestive system disorder|metabolic disease|endocrine system disorder
diseases.definition: Benign recurrent intrahepatic cholestasis 1 (BRIC1) is characterized by episodes of liver dysfunction called cholestasis, during which the liver cells have a reduced ability to release a digestive fluid called bile. diseases.group: hereditary disease|digestive system disorder|metabolic disease|endocrine system disorder
diseases.definition: Benign recurrent intrahepatic cholestasis (BRIC) is a hereditary liver disorder characterized by intermittent episodes of intrahepatic cholestasis, generally without progression to chronic liver damage. diseases.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A non-cancerous nodular enlargement of the prostate gland. It is characterized by the presence of epithelial cell nodules, and stromal nodules containing fibrous and smooth muscle elements. It is the most common urologic disorder in men, causing blockage of urine flow.

diseases.definition: A peritoneal benign neoplasm that is characterized by the presence of prominent hemangiopericytoma-like vessels.

diseases.name: Benign peritoneal mesothelioma

diseases.definition: Benign partial epilepsy with secondarily generalized seizures in infancy is a rare infantile epilepsy syndrome characterized by seizures presenting with motion arrest and staring. They are followed by generalized tonic-clonic convulsions with normal interictal EEG and focal paroxysmal discharges, followed by generalization in ictal EEG. Seizures usually occur in clusters and are responsive to t...

diseases.name: Benign partial epilepsy of infancy with complex partial seizures
diseases.definition: Benign partial epilepsy of infancy with complex partial seizures is a rare infantile epilepsy syndrome characterized by complex partial seizures presenting with motion arrest, decreased responsiveness, staring, automatisms and mild clonic movements, with or without apneas, normal interictal EEG and focal, mostly temporal discharges in ictal EEG. Most often, seizures occur in clusters and have a...

diseases.name: Benign paroxysmal torticollis of infancy
diseases.definition: Benign paroxysmal torticollis of infancy (BPTI) is a rare functional disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of torticollic posturing of the head (inclination or tilting of the head to one side) in healthy children.

diseases.group: hereditary disease|nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system

Bilateral vertical nystagmus is assoc...

diseases.name: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
diseases.group: auditory system disorder|hereditary disease|nervous system disorder|otorhinolaryngologic disease
diseases.definition: Idiopathic recurrent vertigo associated with positional nystagmus. It is associated with a vestibular loss without other neurological or auditory signs. Unlike in labyrinthitis and vestibular neuronitis inflammation in the ear is not observed.

diseases.name: Benign ovarian mucinous tumor
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare disorder that affects women with a history of uterine leiomyoma, which is found to metastasise within extrauterine sites.The disease develops as a proliferation of multiple nodules composed of smooth muscle cells.The most frequent site of metastasis is the lungs, although other areas may also be affected as well, including some atypical locations, e.g. the heart or spinal cord.

diseases.name: Benign mesenchymoma

diseases.name: Benign meningioma
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.group: respiratory system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the larynx. Representative examples include squamous papilloma and hemangioma.

diseases.name: Benign insulitis
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder
diseases.definition: A benign form of insulitis which is an inflammation of the islets of Langerhans of the pancreas. The pancreas and in some cases the Pancreatic β-cells become infiltrated by polymorphonuclear leukocytes and infiltrated by mononuclear cells, leading to inflammation.

diseases.name: Benign infantile seizures associated with mild gastroenteritis
diseases.definition: Benign infantile seizures associated with mild gastroenteritis is a rare infantile epilepsy syndrome characterized by benign afebrile seizures in previously healthy infants and children (age range 1 month to 6 years) with mild acute gastroenteritis without any central nervous system infection, severe dehydration, or electrolyte imbalances. In most cases the seizures are tonic-clonic with focal ...

diseases.name: Benign infantile focal epilepsy with midline spikes and wave during sleep
diseases.definition: Benign infantile focal epilepsy with midline spikes and waves during sleep is a rare infantile epilepsy syndrome characterized by age of onset between 4 and 30 months, partial sporadic seizures presenting with motion arrest, staring, cyanosis and, less common, automatisms and lateralizing signs, and characteristic interictal sleep EEG changes consisting of a spike followed by a bell-shaped slow...

diseases.name: Benign idiopathic neonatal seizures
diseases.definition: A rare neonatal epilepsy syndrome characterized by seizures without specific underlying etiology, occurring during the first days of life in infants with an otherwise normal neurological state and no family history of neonatal convulsions. The most commonly partial and clonic seizures usually last for one to three minutes. Repeated seizures may lead to status epilepticus lasting up to 20 hours....

diseases.name: Benign hypertensive renal disease
synonyms: hypertensive renal disease, benign, without mention of renal failure

diseases.name: Benign focal seizures of adolescence
diseases.definition: A rare epilepsy typically characterized by isolated focal motor and somatosensory seizures. Less frequently other focal seizure types, with or without secondary generalization, have been described. The seizures usually happen when the patient is awake and take a benign course. The condition is transitory, interictal examinations are normal, and there is usually no family history of epilepsy.

diseases.name: Benign familial nocturnal alternating hemiplegia of childhood
synonyms: benign familial nocturnal alternating hemiplegia in childhood
diseases.definition: Benign nocturnal alternating hemiplegia of childhood is a rare neurologic disease characterized by recurrent attacks of nocturnal screaming or crying followed or accompanied by unilateral or sometimes bilateral hemiplegia. Disorder is not associated with neurological or developmental impairments but may be associated with mild behavioral abnormalities.

diseases.name: Benign familial infantile epilepsy
diseases.definition: A genetic epileptic syndrome characterized by the occurrence of afebrile repeated seizures in healthy infants, between the third and eighth month of life.

diseases.name: Benign exophthalmos syndrome
diseases.definition: Benign exophthalmos syndrome is characterized by slowly progressive unilateral exophthalmos and ipsilateral mucosal turbinate hypertrophy, without intraorbital or intranasal lesions.

diseases.name: Benign essential hypertension
diseases.definition: A condition of mild to moderate high blood pressure that has no identifiable cause.

diseases.name: Benign essential blepharospasm
diseases.definition: Involuntary twitching of the eyelid.

diseases.name: Benign epithelial tumor of salivary glands
Benign eccrine breast spiradenoma
synonyms: benign eccrine spiradenoma of the breast
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|breast disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A very rare, benign sweat gland neoplasm that affects the breast. It is characterized by the proliferation of basaloid epithelial cells.

diseases.name: Benign duodenal neoplasm
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A non-metastasizing neoplasm arising from the wall of the duodenum.

diseases.name: Benign dermal neurilemmoma
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Benign deep fibrous histiocytoma
diseases.definition: A rare, well-circumscribed, pseudo-encapsulated benign fibrous histiocytoma that arises entirely within the subcutaneous tissue or deep soft tissue. It usually affects the extremities or the head and neck region. It recurs locally in a minority of cases.

diseases.name: Benign cystic nephroma
diseases.group: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A benign encapsulated neoplasm of the kidney, characterized by the presence of cysts separated by septa. There are no solid areas present. The septa are lined by one layer of epithelial cells that have eosinophilic or clear cytoplasm. The cystic spaces contain serous or hemorrhagic fluid.

diseases.name: Benign conjunctival neoplasm
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: Abnormal growth of the cells of the conjunctiva without malignant characteristics.

diseases.name: Benign concentric annular macular dystrophy
diseases.group: hereditary disease|nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system
diseases.definition: Benign concentric annular macular dystrophy (BCAMD) is a progressive autosomal dominant macular dystrophy characterized by parafoveal hypopigmentation followed by a retinitis pigmentosa-like phenotype (nyctalopia and peripheral vision loss) with a bullBs eye configuration.

diseases.name: Benign carotid body paraganglioma
diseases.group: hereditary disease|nervous system disorder|endocrine system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A carotid body paraganglioma that is confined to the site of origin, without metastatic potential.

diseases.name: Benign breast phyllodes tumor
synonyms: benign phyllodes tumour of the breast
benign phyllodes tumor of the breast
benign phyllodes neoplasm of the breast
diseases.definition: A usually unilateral, benign and well circumscribed biphasic neoplasm that arises from the breast. It usually affects middle-aged women. It is characterized by the presence of a double layer of epithelial cells that are arranged in clefts, surrounded by a cellular, monomorphic spindle cell mesenchymal component. Mitoses are rare. Necrotic changes may be present in large tumors.

diseases.name: Benign breast adenomyoepithelioma
diseases.definition: A benign, nodular tumor that arises from the breast parenchyma. It is characterized by the proliferation of myoepithelial cells around spaces that are lined by epithelial cells. Occasionally, adenomyoepitheliomas may undergo malignant transformation.

diseases.name: Benign basal cell neoplasm
diseases.definition: A neoplasm composed of basal cells that remains localized and does not metastasize to other anatomic sites.

diseases.name: Benign angiitis of the central nervous system
diseases.definition: A central nervous system vasculitis that has a benign course, with acute onset of neurologic symptoms, usually in the form of severe headache and/or a focal neurologic event.

diseases.name: Benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy
synonyms: familial cortical myoclonic tremor and epilepsy
autosomal dominant cortical myoclonus and epilepsy
diseases.definition: Benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy (BAFME) is an inherited epileptic syndrome characterized by cortical hand tremors, myoclonic jerks and occasional generalized or focal seizures with a non-progressive or very slowly progressive disease course, and no signs of early dementia or cerebellar ataxia.

diseases.name: Benign adrenal gland pheochromocytoma
diseases.group: hereditary disease|nervous system disorder|endocrine system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A sporadic or familial pheochromocytoma that is confined to the adrenal gland and does not have any metastatic potential. The majority of cases are sporadic, and usually unilateral. Familial cases are usually bilateral.

diseases.name: Benign samaritan congenital myopathy
diseases.definition: Benign Samaritan congenital myopathy is a rare, genetic, skeletal muscle disease characterized by severe neonatal hypotonia with respiratory insufficiency, delay in motor milestones, and dysmorphic features including bitemporal narrowing, epicanthal folds and hypertelorism. Affected individuals show gradual improvement in hypotonia and muscle weakness within the first two years of life resultin...

diseases.name: Benign leydig cell tumor
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A Leydig cell tumor which does not recur or metastasize. Morphologically, there is no evidence of cellular atypia, increased mitotic activity, necrosis, or vascular invasion.

diseases.name: Bejel
synonyms: Treponema pallidum subsp. endemicum infectious disease
Treponema pallidum subsp. endemicum disease or disorder
Treponema pallidum subsp. endemicum caused disease or disorder
diseases.definition: A chronic skin and tissue disease caused by infection by the endemicum subspecies of the spirochete Treponema pallidum.

diseases.name: Behavioral variant of frontotemporal dementia
diseases.definition: Behavioral variant of frontotemporal dementia (bv-FTD) is a form of frontotemporal dementia (FTD), characterized by progressive behavioral impairment and a decline in executive function with frontal lobe-predominant atrophy.

diseases.name: Baylisascariasis
synonyms: Baylisascaris procyonis caused disease or disorder
diseases.definition: An infection that is caused by the raccoon nematode Baylisascaris procyonis, which is transmitted by the ingestion of embryonated eggs in contaminated soil; symptoms depend on larval migration sites (visceral organs, eye, or brain) provoking severe inflammatory responses.

diseases.name: Bathing suit ichthyosis
diseases.definition: Bathing suit ichthyosis (BSI) is a rare variant of autosomal recessive congenital ichthyosis (ARCI) characterized by the presence of large dark scales in specific areas of the body.

diseases.name: Basosquamous carcinoma
synonyms: skin mixed basal and squamous cell carcinoma
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A basal cell carcinoma which displays squamous differentiation. The neoplastic cells have more abundant cytoplasm with more marked keratinization than typical basal cell carcinomas. It usually has a more aggressive clinical course compared to typical basal cell carcinoma, and it may produce regional or widespread metastases.

diseases.name: Basilar artery insufficiency
diseases.definition: A syndrome which occurs as a result of the occlusion of the basilar artery. It may be caused by atherosclerosis, embolism or hemorrhage. Clinical signs include dizziness, headache, vomiting, hemiparesis or hemiplegia, dysarthria, dysphagia, blurred vision and loss of consciousness. The clinical course is variable and is dependent upon the extent of the occlusion and the location of the clot alo...

diseases.name: Basaloid large cell lung carcinoma
diseases.group: respiratory system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A morphologic variant of large cell lung carcinoma characterized by the presence of a solid nodular or anastomotic trabecular growth pattern, peripheral palisading, and comedo type necrosis.

diseases.name: Basaloid follicular hamartoma
diseases.definition: A type of pilosebaceous hamartoma characterized by basal cell epitheliomata, epidermoid cysts and comedones, and epidermal atrophy.

diseases.name: Basaloid carcinoma of the penis
synonyms: squamous cell carcinoma of the penis, basaloid type
squamous cell carcinoma of penis, basaloid type
basaloid squamous cell carcinoma of the penis
basaloid squamous cell carcinoma of penis
diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An aggressive, human papillomavirus-related squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the penis. It is characterized by the presence of nests of small malignant cells. The malignant cells tend to invade deeply into the adjacent tissues. Comedo-type necrosis is often present.

diseases.name: Basal-like breast carcinoma
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|breast disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A biologic subset of breast carcinoma defined by high expression of genes characteristic of basal epithelial cells, including KRT5 and KRT17, annexin 8, CX3CL1, and TRIM29, and usually by lack of expression of the estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2). It is the most common subtype of breast cancer associated with BRCA1 mutations...

diseases.name: Basal laminar drusen
diseases.group: hereditary disease|cardiovascular disorder|nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system
diseases.definition: A retinal drusen characterized by yellow-white deposits (drusen) that accumulate beneath the retinal pigment epithelium on Bruch membrane and that has material basis in mutations in the CFH gene on chromosome 1q31.3.

diseases.name: Basal ganglia cerebrovascular disorder
synonyms: collection of basal ganglia cerebrovascular disorder
cerebrovascular disorder of collection of basal ganglia
diseases.definition: A pathological condition caused by impaired blood flow in the basal regions of cerebral hemispheres (basal ganglia), such as infarction; hemorrhage; or ischemia in vessels of this brain region including the lateral lenticulostriate arteries. Primary clinical manifestations include involuntary movements (dyskinesias) and muscle weakness (hemiparesis).

diseases.name: Baroreflex failure
diseases.definition: Baroreflex failure is a rare disorder that causes fluctuations in blood pressure with episodes of severe hypertension (high blood pressure) and elevated heart rate in response to stress, exercise, and pain. Individuals may also have hypotension (low blood pressure) with normal or reduced heart rate during periods of rest. Symptoms of baroreflex failure may include headache, sweating, and a hear...

diseases.name: Baritosis
diseases.definition: A rare type of pneumoconiosis caused by long standing exposure to barium dust. It is characterized by the formation of fine dense lesions in the lung parenchyma. The lesions do not affect the lung function and disappear without treatment after the exposure to barium dust stops.

diseases.name: Bardet-biedl syndrome 21
diseases.definition: BBS21 is an autosomal recessive ciliopathy characterized by obesity, postaxial polydactyly, retinal degeneration, and mild cognitive impairment ({1:Heon et al., 2016}; {2:Khan et al., 2016}).nnFor a general phenotypic description and a discussion of genetic heterogeneity of Bardet-Biedl syndrome, see BBS1 (OMIM:209900).

diseases.name: Barbiturate dependence
diseases.definition: A drug dependence that involves the continued use of barbiturates despite problems related to use of the substance.

diseases.name: Barbiturate abuse
diseases.definition: A substance abuse that involves the recurring use of barbiturate drugs despite negative consequences.

diseases.name: Band keratopathy
diseases.definition: The deposition of calcium on the cornea, resulting in pain and decreased visual acuity.

diseases.name: Balloon cell malignant melanoma
synonyms: balloon cell malignant melanoma of the skin
balloon cell malignant melanoma of skin
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A rare variant of melanoma with a vertical growth phase. It presents as a nodular or polypoid skin lesion. It is characterized by the presence of nodules which contain large melanoma cells with clear, foamy or finely vacuolated cytoplasm. The prognosis is similar to that of other melanomas matched for depth of invasion.

diseases.name: Balantidiasis
diseases.definition: Infection by parasites of the genus balantidium. The presence of Balantidium in the large intestine leads to diarrhea; dysentery; and occasionally ulcer.

diseases.name: Balanitis xerotica obliterans
diseases.definition: A chronic and progressive inflammatory process that affects the glans penis and the foreskin. It presents with white atrophic patches in the glans of penis and foreskin and it is often associated with the development of a sclerotic, whitish ring in the tip of the foreskin that may lead to phimosis. It is also known as lichen sclerosus of the penis.

diseases.name: Balanitis
diseases.definition: An infectious or non-infectious inflammatory process that affects the glans penis. Symptoms include redness and pain of the glans penis and foreskin and discharge.

diseases.name: Balanced robertsonian translocation down syndrome
diseases.definition: Robertsonian translocation Down syndrome in which translocation displacement of the end regions of chromosomes occurred without loss of chromosomal material between the two nonhomologous chromosomes.

diseases.name: Baker vinters syndrome
diseases.definition: A very rare syndrome characterized by craniosynostosis (premature fusion of skull bones), hydrocephalus (an abnormal increase of cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles of the brain) and abnormal development of the channel or duct in the middle of the brain that connects the third and fourth ventricles. This is an n-of-1 use case where only one patient or family has been described with this disor...

diseases.name: Bagassosis
diseases.group: immune system disorder|respiratory system disorder|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: An occupational lung disorder caused by inhalation of bagasse dust. In the acute phase, it manifests as cough, dyspnea, fever, chills, and weakness. Chronic exposure may lead to interstitial lung fibrosis.

diseases.name: Bacteriuria
diseases.definition: The presence of bacteria in the urine which is normally bacteria-free. These bacteria are from the urinary tract and are not contaminants of the surrounding tissues. Bacteriuria can be symptomatic or asymptomatic. Significant bacteriuria is an indicator of urinary tract infection.

diseases.name: Bacterial vaginosis
diseases.definition: Infection caused by bacterial overgrowth in the vagina. Most affected women are asymptomatic. When symptoms occur, they include foul-smelling vaginal discharge, vaginal itching, and burning. Risk factors include sexual activity with multiple partners and the use of vaginal douches and intrauterine devices. Up to a third of cases resolve without treatment. Antibiotic treatment is recommended whe...

diseases.name: Bacterial myocarditis
diseases.definition: Myocarditis that is caused by an infection with a bacterial agent.

diseases.name: Bacterial gastritis
diseases.definition: Gastritis resulting from bacteria.

diseases.name: Bacterial exanthem

diseases.name: Bacterial esophagitis
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|infectious disease|inflammatory disease|upper digestive tract disorder
diseases.definition: An acute bacterial infection that affects the esophagus. Symptoms include severe pain on swallowing and retrosternal pain. Endoscopic examination reveals esophageal mucosal ulcerations and pseudomembranous formations.

diseases.name: Bacterial endocarditis
diseases.definition: Endocarditis that is caused by an infection with a bacterial agent.

diseases.name: Baclofen withdrawal syndrome
diseases.definition: Withdrawal syndrome involving the abrupt discontinuation of baclofen therapy (intrathecal or oral). Baclofen withdrawal syndrome can result in high fever, altered mental status (including agitation, insomnia, confusion, delusions, hallucinations, seizures, visual changes, or psychosis), and potentially profound muscular rigidity that sometimes progresses to fatal rhabdomyolysis.

diseases.name: Bacillary angiomatosis
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|cardiovascular disorder|infectious disease|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A condition that is caused by infection with Bartonella, and which is characterized by vascular proliferation, usually in immunocompromised individuals.

diseases.name: Babesiosis
diseases.definition: Babesiosis refers to a condition caused by microscopic parasites that infect the red blood cells. Many people who are infected with Babesia parasites do not experience any symptoms of the condition. When present, signs and symptoms may include flu-like symptoms such as fever, chills, headache, body aches, nausea and fatigue. In severe cases, babesiosis can be associated with hemolytic anemia. diseases.definition: An eating disorder characterized by avoidance or restriction of food intake due to one or more of the following: lack of interest in eating or food, sensitivity to sensory characteristics of food (such as taste, texture, smell, or appearance), or concern about aversive consequences of eating (such as choking or vomiting), resulting in persistent failure to meet appropriate nutritional and/or en...

diseases.name: Avoidant personality disorder
diseases.definition: A disorder characterized by an enduring pattern of avoidance of social situations and interpersonal contact due to overwhelming feelings of social inadequacy and a hypersensitivity to negative evaluation or rejection.

diseases.name: Avian influenza
diseases.definition: Infection of domestic and wild fowl and other birds with influenza A virus. Avian influenza usually does not sicken birds, but can be highly pathogenic and fatal in domestic poultry.

diseases.definition: Autosomal recessive spondylocostal dysostosis (ARSD) is a rare condition of variable severity associated with vertebral and rib segmentation defects and characterized by a short neck with limited mobility, winged scapulae, a short trunk, and short stature with multiple vertebral anomalies at all levels of the spine.

diseases.definition: Spinocerebellar ataxia autosomal recessive 7, also called SCAR7, is a slowly progressive hereditary form of spinocerebellar ataxia. CMT2M is characterized by congenital ptosis and early cataract associated to a mildly progressive peripheral neuropathy of variable onset from birth to the 6th decade, pes cavus, reduced to absent ankles tendon reflexes and sometimes neutropenia.

diseases.definition: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, type 2K (CMT2K) is an axonal CMT peripheral sensorimotor polyneuropathy.

diseases.definition: Agammaglobulinemia, non-Bruton type (autosomal agammaglobulinemia) is a rare form of agammaglobulinemia, a primary immunodeficiency disease, and is characterized by variable immune dysfunction with frequent and recurrent bacterial infections and/or chronic diarrhea.

diseases.name: Autoinflammatory syndrome due to tbk1 deficiency

diseases.group: immune system disorder|nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system|otorhinolaryngologic disease

diseases.name: Autoimmune pulmonary disease due to pd-1 deficiency
diseases.definition: An autoimmune disease that is characterized by a lack of PD-1 on patient peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and reduced IFN production in response to mycobacterial stimuli.

diseases.name: Autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis
diseases.definition: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP) is a rare lung disease characterized by the accumulation of a lipoproteinaceous substance in the distal air spaces which positively stains with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS).

diseases.name: Autoimmune polyendocrinopathy type 2
synonyms: autoimmune thyroid disease and/or type 1 diabetes-Addison disease syndrome
diseases.group: syndromic disease|immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder

diseases.name: Autoimmune polyendocrinopathy
diseases.group: syndromic disease|immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder
diseases.definition: A group of diverse conditions that are characterized by spontaneous, multi-organ autoimmunity, which target both endocrine (adrenal, gonad, pancreatic islet cells, parathyroid, pituitary, thyroid) and non-endocrine (gastrointestinal, integumentary, lymphatic) tissues.

diseases.name: Autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1

autoimmune polyendocrinopathy caused by mutation in aire
autoimmune polyendocrinopathy caused by mutation in AIRE

diseases.name: Duct-centric pancreatitis
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: Type 2 autoimmune pancreatitis is a form of autoimmune pancreatitis (see this term) affecting both sexes and having a younger age of onset (60 years) and presenting with abdominal pain, steatorrhea and obstructive jaundice.

diseases.name: Lymphoplasmacytic sclerosing pancreatitis
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: Type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis is a form of autoimmune pancreatitis seen in elderly males (60 years) and presenting with abdominal pain, steatorrhea, obstructive jaundice and other organ (bile duct, kidneys and retroperitoneum) involvement. It is thought to be due to an immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4)-associated systemic disease.

diseases.name: Autoimmune optic neuritis

diseases.definition: An autoimmune form of optic neuritis.

diseases.group: reproductive system disorder|immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: Autoimmune oophoritis is a rare cause of primary ovarian insufficiency (POI). It happens when the body's immune system mistakenly attacks the ovaries causing inflammation, atrophy and fibrosis. These changes stop the ovaries from working normally. diseases.name: Autoimmune neuropathy
diseases.definition: An autoimmune form of peripheral neuropathy.

diseases.name: Autoimmune myocarditis
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|cardiovascular disorder|immune system disorder|inflammatory disease

diseases.name: Autoimmune limbic encephalitis
diseases.group: immune system disorder|nervous system disorder|inflammatory disease
diseases.definition: A rare autoimmune encephalitis involving the mesial temporal lobes and clinically characterized by subacute onset (i. e. rapid progression of less than three months) of short-term memory deficits, seizures or psychiatric symptoms, such as behavioral changes, anxiety, depression, and psychosis. Further diagnostic criteria are bilateral abnormalities restricted to the mesial temporal lobes in bra...

diseases.name: Autoimmune interstitial lung disease-arthritis syndrome

diseases.name: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia
diseases.definition: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) is an autoimmune disorder in which various types of auto-antibodies are directed against red blood cells causing their survival to be shortened and resulting in hemolytic anemia.

diseases.name: Autoimmune glomerulonephritis

diseases.definition: Inflammation of the body fundic mucosa of the stomach. It results from the development of autoantibodies against the parietal and chief cells. It is associated with the presence of intestinal metaplasia and an increased risk of developing gastric carcinoma.

diseases.name: Autoimmune epilepsy
diseases.definition: An epilepsy that is characterized by new-onset refractory seizures along with subacute progressive cognitive decline and behavioral or psychiatric dysfunction.

Autoimmune disease

diseases.name: Autoimmune atherosclerosis

diseases.name: Auto-brewery syndrome
diseases.definition: An acquired metabolic disease that is characterized by the endogenous production of ethanol produced through endogenous fermentation by fungi or bacteria in the gastrointestinal system, oral cavity, or urinary system and typically presents with the signs of alcohol intoxication.

diseases.name: Autism-facial port-wine stain syndrome
diseases.definition: This syndrome is characterized by the presence of a unilateral angioma on the face and autistic developmental problems characterized by language delay and atypical social interactions.

diseases.name: Autism spectrum disorder 3
diseases.definition: The most severe form of autism spectrum disorder, characterized by severe impairments in social communication and extreme restricted, repetitive behaviors, requiring very substantial support for daily functioning.

diseases.name: Autism spectrum disorder 2
diseases.definition: A moderate form of autism spectrum disorder marked by more significant challenges in social communication and more noticeable restricted, repetitive behaviors, requiring substantial support for daily functioning.

diseases.name: Autism spectrum disorder 1

diseases.name: Autism spectrum disorder
synonyms: pervasive developmental disorder - not otherwise specified

diseases.name: Auriculoosteodysplasia
diseases.definition: Auriculoosteodysplasia is a very rare condition characterized by multiple osseous dysplasia, characteristic ear shape (elongation of the lobe that is attached and accompanied by a small, slightly posterior lobule) and somewhat short stature.

diseases.definition: Auriculo-condylar syndrome (ACS) presents with bilateral external ear malformations ('question mark' ears), mandibular condyle hypoplasia, microstomia, micrognathia, microglossia and facial asymmetry. Additional manifestations include hypotonia, ptosis, cleft palate, puffy cheeks, developmental delay, impaired hearing and respiratory distress.

diseases.name: Auricular abnormalities-cleft lip with or without cleft palate-ocular abnormalities syndrome
diseases.definition: The association of auricular abnormalities and cleft lip with or without cleft palate has been described in two siblings. One sibling had postauricular pits, profound myopia, nystagmus and retinal pigment abnormalities. The second sibling was a fetus (gestational age: 23 weeks) with severe cleft lip, cleft palate and external ear abnormalities.

diseases.name: Auditory system benign neoplasm

diseases.definition: Audiogenic seizures is a rare neurologic disease characterized by seizures that are triggered by acoustic stimulation, which can be simple (as in startle epilepsy) or complex (e.g. musicogenic seizures, seizures triggered by the voice).

diseases.definition: Atypical juvenile parkinsonism (AJP) is a complex form of young-onset Parkinson disease (YOPD) that manifests with pyramidal signs, eye movement abnormalities, psychiatric manifestations (depression, anxiety, drug-induced psychosis, and impulse control disorders), intellectual disability, and other neurological symptoms (such as ataxia and epilepsy) along with classical parkinsonian symptoms.

diseases.definition: This syndrome is characterized by progressive ataxia beginning during childhood, deafness and intellectual deficit.

diseases.group: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.group: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Astigmatism
diseases.definition: Unequal curvature of the refractive surfaces of the eye. Thus a point source of light cannot be brought to a point focus on the retina but is spread over a more or less diffuse area. This results from the radius of curvature in one plane being longer or shorter than the radius at right angles to it. (Dorland, 27th ed)

diseases.name: Asternia
diseases.definition: Asternia, also known as a complete congenital sternal cleft, is a condition in which a bone called thesternum does not form properly.The sternumusuallyconnects to the ribs to form the ribcage. Individuals with asternia are missing this bone and may appear to have a rut or trench under the skin in the middle of the chest. Most individuals with asternia have no symptoms, though some may have diff...

diseases.name: Astereognosia
diseases.definition: An agnosia that is the loss of the ability to recognize objects by touch based on its texture, size and weight.

diseases.name: Associative visual agnosia

diseases.name: Aspiration pneumonia

diseases.name: Aseptic meningitis
diseases.definition: Inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord without a bacterial pathogen.

diseases.name: Ascariasis

diseases.name: Asbestosis
diseases.definition: A lung disorder caused by inhalation of asbestos fibers. It results in fibrosis of the lung parenchyma. Signs and symptoms include coughing, shortness of breath and chest pain.

diseases.definition: Aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase deficiency is a very rare, severe, genetic neurometabolic disorder associated with clinical manifestations related to underproduction of serotonin and dopamine, mainly hypotonia, hypokinesia, ptosis oculogyric crises, and signs of autonomic dysfunction.

diseases.name: Aromatase excess syndrome
synonyms: gynecomastia, familial, due to increased aromatase activity
diseases.definition: Aromatase excess syndrome is a rare, genetic endocrine disease characterized by increased levels of estrogen due to elevated extraglandular aromatase activity. Males present with heterosexual precocious puberty which manifests with pre- or peripubertal onset of gynecomastia, premature growth spurt, accelerated bone maturation resulting in decreased adult stature, and may present mild hypogonado...

diseases.name: Aromatase deficiency
diseases.group: hereditary disease|reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|obstetric disorder
diseases.definition: Aromatase deficiency disrupts the synthesis of estradiol, resulting in hirsutism of mothers during gestation of an affected child; pseudohermaphroditism and virilization in women; and tall stature, osteoporosis and obesity in men.

diseases.name: Ariboflavinosis
diseases.definition: A dietary deficiency of riboflavin causing a syndrome chiefly marked by cheilitis, angular stomatitis, glossitis associated with a purplish red or magenta-colored tongue that may show fissures, corneal vascularization, dyssebacia, and anemia. (Dorland, 27th ed)

diseases.name: Bosma arhinia microphthalmia syndrome
synonyms: hyposmia-nasal and ocular hypoplasia-hypogonadotropic hypogonadism syndrome
diseases.group: hereditary disease|reproductive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Any syndromic disease characterized by severe hypoplasia of the nose and eyes, palatal abnormalities, deficient taste and smell, inguinal hernias, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with cryptorchidism, and normal intelligence that occurs due to variation in the SMCHD1 gene.

diseases.name: argyrophilic grain disease
diseases.definition: A tauopathy characterized pathologically by the presence of silver stain positive lesions called argyrophilic grains, oligodendrocytic coiled bodies, and neuronal tau-positive pretangles.

diseases.name: Argyria
diseases.definition: Argyria is a rare dermatosis, which can be either localized or systemic, that occurs after prolonged contact and absorption of silver containing compounds over a period of years and that is characterized by irreversible blue-gray to gray-black staining of skin, fingernails and/or mucous membranes, most evident on sun exposed areas of the skin. Silver exposure is usually occupational but may als...

diseases.name: Argininosuccinic aciduria
diseases.definition: Argininosuccinic aciduria (ASA) is a disorder of urea cycle metabolism most commonly characterized by either a severe, neonatal-onset form that manifests with hyperammonemia accompanied with vomiting, hypothermia, lethargy and poor feeding in the first few days of life, or late-onset forms (any age outside the newborn period) that manifest with stress or infection-induced episodic hyperammonemi...

diseases.name: Arginase deficiency
diseases.definition: Arginase deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive amino acid metabolism disorder characterized clinically by variable degrees of hyperammonemia, developing from about 3 years of age, and leading to progressive loss of developmental milestones and spasticity in the absence of treatment.

diseases.name: Aregenerative anemia
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor

diseases.name: Arcus senilis
diseases.definition: A corneal disease in which there is a deposition of phospholipid and cholesterol in the corneal stroma and anterior sclera.

diseases.name: Arbovirus infection
diseases.definition: A viral infection that is transmitted by an arthropod.

diseases.name: Arakawa syndrome 2
diseases.definition: A rare autosomal dominant inherited metabolic disorder characterized by deficiency of the enzyme tetrahydrofolate-methyltransferase. It results in the abnormal metabolism of methylcobalamin. Signs and symptoms include mental retardation, megaloblastic anemia, hypotonia, epilepsy, and hepatosplenomegaly.

diseases.name: Arachnoiditis
diseases.definition: Arachnoiditis (ARC) is a chronic inflammation of the arachnoid layer of the meninges, of which adhesive arachnoiditis is the most severe form, characterized by debilitating, intractable neurogenic back and limb pain and a range of other neurological problems.

diseases.name: Arachnoid cyst
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Intracranial or spinal cavities containing a cerebrospinal-like fluid, the wall of which is composed of arachnoidal cells. They are most often developmental or related to trauma. Intracranial arachnoid cysts usually occur adjacent to arachnoidal cistern and may present with hydrocephalus; headache; seizures; and focal neurologic signs. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1994, Ch44, pp105-115)

diseases.name: Arachnodactyly-intellectual disability-dysmorphism syndrome
diseases.group: syndromic disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Arachnodactyly-intellectual disability-dysmorphism syndrome is characterized by moderate intellectual deficit, brachycephaly, typical facies (thin lips and microstomia), ectomorphic habitus with extremely long, thin fingers and toes, and hypoplastic external genitalia. It has been described in three patients.

diseases.name: Arachnodactyly-abnormal ossification-intellectual disability syndrome
diseases.definition: Arachnodactyly - abnormal ossification - intellectual disability is a multiple congenital developmental anomalies syndrome characterized by arachnodactyly of fingers and toes associated with craniofacial dysmorphism (including abnormal cranial ossification, frontal bossing, flat calvaria, shallow deformed orbits resulting in exophtalmos, midface hypoplasia and micrognathia), feeding difficultie...

diseases.name: Aquarium granuloma
diseases.definition: A skin condition caused by Mycobacterium marinum, characterized by a skin lesion that presents roughly three weeks after exposure.

diseases.name: Aquagenic pruritus
diseases.definition: Aquagenic pruritus is a conditionin which contact with water of any temperature causes intense itching, without any visible skin changes. The symptoms may begin immediately after contact and can last for an hour or more. The cause of aquagenic pruritus is unknown; however, familial cases have been described. It may be a symptom of polycythemia vera or another underlying condition. Overall, trea...

diseases.name: Aquagenic palmoplantar keratoderma
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Aquagenic syringeal acrokeratoderma is a rare condition affecting the palms of the hands. It is characterized by the appearance or worsening of a palmar eruption, following brief exposure to water. The palmar eruption is made up of small, white or shining pimples that can conjoin into plaques. The feet are unaffected. Symptoms include a burning pain and a tightening sensation in the palms, as w...

diseases.name: Aprosencephaly cerebellar dysgenesis
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Aprosencephaly
diseases.group: nervous system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Apraxia
diseases.definition: Apraxia is a neurological disorder characterized by the inability to perform tasks or movements, despite having the desire and physical ability to perform them. It is caused by damage to the brain, especially the parietal lobe, and can arise from many diseases, tumors, a stroke, or traumatic brain injury. In some cases it is present from birth. There are several types of apraxia, which may occu...

diseases.name: Apperceptive agnosia
diseases.group: psychiatric disorder|nervous system disorder|disorder of visual system
diseases.definition: An agnosia that is a loss of the ability to distinguish visual shapes.

diseases.name: Appendix villous adenoma
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An adenoma arising from the appendix. It is characterized by the presence of villous epithelial structures and it is associated with dysplasia.

diseases.name: Appendix neuroendocrine tumor g1
synonyms: vermiform appendix neuroendocrine tumor, well differentiated, low grade
grade 1 neuroendocrine neoplasm of vermiform appendix
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A well differentiated, low grade tumor with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the appendix. The mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 HPF and/or the Ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.

diseases.name: Appendix mucinous cystadenocarcinoma
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: An adenocarcinoma arising from the appendix, characterized by the presence of mucinous stroma formation and cystic structures.

diseases.name: Appendix lymphoma
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A lymphoma arising from the appendix. The majority of lymphomas affecting the appendix represent disease extension from the intestinal wall; primary lymphomas of the appendix are rare.

diseases.name: Appendix leiomyoma
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|digestive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A well-circumscribed benign smooth muscle neoplasm arising from the appendix. It is characterized by the presence of spindle cells with cigar-shaped nuclei, interlacing fascicles, and a whorled pattern.

diseases.name: Appendix hyperplastic polyp
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A non-neoplastic polyp that arises from the appendix. It is characterized by the presence of elongated serrated crypts and the absence of atypia or dysplasia.

diseases.name: Appendix cancer
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A malignant neoplasm involving the vermiform appendix

diseases.name: Appendix l-cell glucagon-like peptide-producing neuroendocrine tumor
synonyms: vermiform appendix L-cell glucagon-like peptide-producing neuroendocrine tumour
vermiform appendix L-cell glucagon-like peptide-producing neuroendocrine tumor
malignant appendiceal L-cell glucagon-like peptide producing tumour
malignant appendiceal L-cell glucagon-like peptide producing tumor
appendix L-cell glucagon-like peptide-producing neuroendocrine tumor
L-cell glucagon-like peptide-producing neuroendocrine tumour of vermiform appendix
L-cell glucagon-like peptide-producing neuroendocrine tumor of vermiform appendix
diseases.group: digestive system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor
diseases.definition: A neuroendocrine tumor arising from the wall of the appendix, producing glucagon-like peptides. Morphologically, it is characterized by the presence of neoplastic cells forming tubular or trabecular patterns.

diseases.name: Appendicitis
diseases.definition: Acute inflammation of the vermiform appendix.

diseases.name: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|metabolic disease|endocrine system disorder
diseases.definition: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess (AME) is a rare form of pseudohyperaldosteronism characterized by very early-onset and severe hypertension, associated with low renin levels and hypoaldosteronism.

diseases.name: Apolipoprotein a-ii amyloidosis
synonyms: hereditary renal amyloidosis due to apolipoprotein A-II variant
hereditary amyloid nephropathy due to apolipoprotein A-II variant
familial renal amyloidosis due to apolipoprotein A-II variant
familial amyloid nephropathy due to apolipoprotein A-II variant

diseases.name: apolipoprotein A-I deficiency
diseases.definition: A lipoprotein metabolism disorder characterized biochemically by complete absence of apolipoprotein AI and extremely low plasma high density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol, and clinically by corneal opacities and xanthomas complicated with premature coronary heart disease (CHD).

diseases.name: Apodia, unilateral
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Apodia, bilateral
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|hereditary disease|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Apocrine adenosis of breast
diseases.definition: Breast adenosis characterized by the presence of extensive apocrine metaplasia.

diseases.name: Apnea of prematurity
diseases.definition: Apnea of prematurity is a developmental disorder affecting premature infants, likely secondary to an immaturity of respiratory control resulting in idiopathic pauses in breathing often associated with reduced heart rate and arterial blood oxygen levels. It may be exacerbated by concurrent neonatal diseases.

diseases.name: Aplastic anemia
diseases.definition: Anemia resulting from bone marrow failure (aplastic or hypoplastic bone marrow). The production of erythroblasts and red cells is markedly decreased, and it may be associated with decreased production of granulocytes (granulocytopenia) and platelets (thrombocytopenia) as well. Aplastic anemia may be idiopathic or secondary due to bone marrow damage by toxins, radiation, or immunologic factors.

diseases.name: Aplasia of lacrimal and salivary glands
synonyms: congenital absence of lacrimal puncta and salivary glands
aplasia of lacrimal and salivary glands
diseases.definition: Aplasia of the lacrimal and salivary glands (ALSG) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder characterized by aplasia, atresia or hypoplasia of the lacrimal and salivary glands leading to varying features since infancy such as recurrent eye infections, irritable eyes, epiphora, xerostomia, dental caries, dental erosion and oral inflammation.

diseases.name: Aplasia cutis-myopia syndrome
diseases.definition: Aplasia cutis-myopia syndrome is characterized by the association of aplasia cutis congenita with high myopia, congenital nystagmus and cone-rod dysfunction. It has been described in two siblings (brother and sister). Transmission is autosomal dominant.

diseases.name: Aplasia cutis-enamel dysplasia syndrome
synonyms: Congenital scalp aplasia cutis-enamel hypoplasia-developmental delay-intellectual disability syndrome

diseases.name: Aplasia cutis congenita-intestinal lymphangiectasia syndrome
diseases.group: integumentary system disorder|syndromic disease|digestive system disorder|immune system disorder
diseases.definition: Aplasia cutis congenita - intestinal lymphangiectasia is an extremely rare association syndrome, described in only two brothers to date (one of which died at 2 months of age), characterized by aplasia cutis congenita of the vertex and generalized edema (as well as hypoproteinemia and lymphopenia) due to intestinal lymphangiectasia. There have been no further descriptions in the literature since...

diseases.name: Aplasia cutis congenita dominant
diseases.definition: Aplasia cutis congenita with with autosomal dominant inheritance with reduced penetrance.

diseases.name: Aplasia cutis congenita
diseases.definition: Aplasia cutis congenita (ACC) is a rare skin disorder characterized by localized absence of skin that is usually located on the scalp but can occur anywhere on the body including the face, trunk and extremities. ACC may occasionally be associated with other anomalies.

diseases.name: Aplasia cutis autosomal recessive
diseases.definition: Aplasia cutis with autosomal recessive inheritance.

diseases.name: Apical myocardial infarction
diseases.definition: An electrocardiographic finding of an injury in leads corresponding to the anatomic region of the apex of the heart.

diseases.name: Aphthous stomatitis
diseases.definition: A recurrent disease of the oral mucosa of unknown etiology. It is characterized by small white ulcerative lesions, single or multiple, round or oval, lasting for 7-14 days and healing without scarring.

diseases.name: Aphonia-deafness-retinal dystrophy-bifid halluces-intellectual disability syndrome
synonyms: aphonia-hearing loss-retinal dystrophy-duplicated halluces-intellectual disability syndrome
diseases.definition: Aphonia-deafness-retinal dystrophy-bifid halluces-intellectual disability syndrome is a rare, genetic, multiple congenital anomalies/dysmorphic syndrome characterized by moderate to severe intellectual disability, congenital aphonia, hearing loss, optic atrophy, retinal dystrophy, broad thumbs and duplicated halluces. Facial dysmorphism (incl. thick eyebrows, ptosis, long, downslanting palpebra...

diseases.name: Aphasia
diseases.definition: A language disorder that involves an acquired impairment of any language modality such as producing or comprehending spoken or written language.

diseases.name: Aphalangy-syndactyly-microcephaly syndrome
synonyms: Aphalangia, partial, with syndactyly and Duplication of metatarsal type 4
diseases.group: musculoskeletal system disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Aphalangy-syndactyly-microcephaly is an extremely rare malformation syndrome characterized by the association of partial distal aphalangia with syndactyly, duplication of metatarsal IV, microcephaly, and mild intellectual disability.

diseases.name: Aortopulmonary window
diseases.definition: A rare, congenital anomaly in the aorta in which a communication exists between the ascending aorta and the pulmonary artery.

diseases.name: Aortopulmonary coronary arterial course
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Aortopulmonary coronary arterial course is a rare coronary artery congenital malformation characterized by anomalous origin of the coronary artery from the contralateral sinus of Valsalva with course between the aorta and the pulmonary artery. The anomaly is associated with increased risk of sudden cardiac death, especially during exercise.

diseases.name: Aorto-ventricular tunnel
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Aorto-ventricular tunnel is a congenital, extracardiac channel which connects the ascending aorta above the sinotubular junction to the cavity of the left, or (less commonly) right ventricle.

diseases.name: Aorto-right ventricular tunnel
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Aorto-left ventricular tunnel
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Aortitis
diseases.definition: Inflammation of the aorta. Causes include trauma, infectious disorders, and connective tissue disorders.

diseases.name: Aortic valve stenosis
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Aortic valve stenosis (AVS) is a condition characterized by narrowing of the heart's aortic valve opening. This narrowing prevents the valve from opening fully, which obstructs blood flow from the heart into the aorta, and onward to the rest of the body. AVS can range from mild to severe. Signs and symptoms typically develop when the narrowing of the opening is severe and may include chest pain...

diseases.name: Aortic valve prolapse
diseases.definition: The downward displacement of the cuspal or pointed end of the trileaflet aortic valve causing misalignment of the cusps. Severe valve distortion can cause leakage and allow the backflow of blood from the ascending aorta back into the left ventricle, leading to aortic regurgitation.

diseases.name: Aortic valve insufficiency
diseases.definition: Dysfunction of the aortic valve characterized by incomplete valve closure.

diseases.name: Aortic valve dysplasia
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis

diseases.name: Aortic valve disease 3
diseases.group: hereditary disease|cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Any aortic valve disease characterized by aortic stenosis and/or bicuspid aortic valve in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ROBO4 gene.

diseases.name: Aortic valve disease 2
synonyms: aortic valve disease caused by mutation in SMAD6
diseases.group: hereditary disease|cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Any aortic valve disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the SMAD6 gene.

diseases.name: Aortic valve disease 1
synonyms: aortic valve disease caused by mutation in Notch1
aortic valve disease caused by mutation in NOTCH1
diseases.group: syndromic disease|hereditary disease|cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Any aortic valve disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the NOTCH1 gene.

diseases.name: Aortic valve calcification
diseases.definition: Calcification of the aortic valve

diseases.name: Aortic valve atresia
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: A rare congenital heart defect characterized by the complete failure of the aortic valve to open. It is manifested during infancy with cyanosis, dyspnea, and rapidly progressing heart failure.

diseases.name: Aortic dissection lentiginosis
diseases.definition: A syndrome characterized by arterial dissections, multiple lentigines, and cystic medial necrosis.

diseases.name: Aortic atherosclerosis
diseases.definition: A atherosclerosis that involves the aorta.

diseases.name: Aortic arch interruption, facial palsy, and retinal coloboma
synonyms: aortic arch interruption, facial palsy, and retinal coloboma

diseases.name: Aortic arch interruption
diseases.group: cardiovascular disorder|disorder of development or morphogenesis
diseases.definition: Aortic arch interruption is a rare heart defect characterized by complete lack of anatomical continuity between the transverse aortic arch and the descending thoracic aorta. AAI should be distinguished anatomically from atresia of the aortic arch where continuity between these segments is achieved by an imperforate fibrous strand of various lengths.

diseases.name: Aortic arch anomaly-facial dysmorphism-intellectual disability syndrome
diseases.definition: Aortic arch anomaly-peculiar facies-intellectual disability syndrome is a developmental anomaly characterized at birth by the presence of right-sided aortic arch, craniofacial dysmorphism (microcephaly, asymmetric, facial bones, broad forehead, borderline hypertelorism, nasal septum deviation, large nasal cavity, large, posteriorly rotated ears, and microstomia with downturned corners), and int...

synonyms: familial thoracic aortic aneurysm and aortic dissection caused by mutation in MFAP5
MFAP5 familial thoracic aortic aneurysm and aortic dissection
diseases.definition: Any familial thoracic aortic aneurysm and aortic dissection in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the MFAP5 gene.

diseases.name: Aortic aneurysm, familial thoracic 8
synonyms: familial thoracic aortic aneurysm and aortic dissection caused by mutation in PRKG1
PRKG1 familial thoracic aortic aneurysm and aortic dissection

diseases.name: Aortic aneurysm, familial thoracic 6

ACTA2 familial thoracic aortic aneurysm and aortic dissection
diseases.definition: Any familial thoracic aortic aneurysm and aortic dissection in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ACTA2 gene.

MYH11 familial thoracic aortic aneurysm and aortic dissection
